definition_zh: 物理学家；物理学研究者
definition_en: a person who studies or is trained in physics, either as a researcher or as a teacher
core_image: 一位研究者站在写满公式的黑板前，手里握着粉笔，桌上摆着被拆开的旧钟表与一块磁铁
scene: 研究所的走廊里，一位研究者正把新的测量结果贴到公告板上，同行围过来争论误差来源。 A researcher pinned a new set of measurements to the board in the corridor, and colleagues gathered to argue about the source of error that the physicist had reported.
sceneCN: 这里指「以物理学为专业的研究者」，对应第 1 个义项：从事物理研究的人；句意为研究者把测量结果贴到公告板，同行围绕误差来源展开争论。画面要点：黑板上的公式、粉笔、拆开的钟表与磁铁；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A researcher of matter and energy
senses.titleCN: 研究物质与能量的研究者
senses.definition: a person whose work is to study matter, motion, energy and the forces between them
senses.definitionCN: 以研究物质、运动、能量及其间的作用力为工作的人
senses.example: A researcher pinned a new set of measurements to the board in the corridor, and colleagues gathered to argue about the source of error that the physicist had reported.
senses.exampleCN: 一位研究者把新的测量结果贴到走廊的公告板上，同行围过来争论他所报告的误差来源。
senses.why: The word joins the name of the discipline to a suffix for a practitioner, so it names a person by the field he works in.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把学科名称与表从业者的后缀连在一起，因此它用一个人所从事的领域来命名他。

senses.title: The theorist
senses.definition: one who works mainly with mathematical models and predictions rather than with apparatus
senses.definitionCN: 主要用数学模型与预测工作、而不是与仪器打交道的人
senses.example: The theorist predicted a particle years before it was detected.
senses.exampleCN: 这位理论物理学家在粒子被探测到之前多年就预言了它。
senses.why: The discipline divides between those who write the equations and those who test them, and the same title covers both.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科分成写方程的人与检验方程的人，而同一个称谓覆盖两者。

senses.title: The experimentalist
senses.definition: one who designs instruments and measurements to test predictions or discover new effects
senses.definitionCN: 设计仪器与测量、以检验预言或发现新效应的人
senses.example: The experimentalist spent a decade building the detector.
senses.exampleCN: 这位实验物理学家花了十年建造探测器。
senses.why: A prediction that no one can measure remains a guess, so the title also belongs to the person who builds the test.
senses.whyCN: 无人能测量的预言仍然只是猜测，因此这个称谓也属于搭建检验的人。

senses.title: A specialist in a branch
senses.definition: a person who works in a named branch such as astrophysics, geophysics or particle physics
senses.definitionCN: 在天体物理、地球物理或粒子物理等具名分支中工作的人
senses.example: The astrophysicist studies how galaxies collide.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天体物理学家研究星系如何碰撞。
senses.why: The title combines with branch prefixes, so it multiplies into as many names as the subject has branches.
senses.whyCN: 这个称谓可以与分支前缀组合，因此它随学科的分支数量一同增殖。

senses.title: A teacher of the subject
senses.definition: a person who teaches physics in a school or university rather than working mainly in a laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学教物理、而非主要在实验室工作的人
senses.example: The physicist who taught the evening class wrote his own demonstrations.
senses.exampleCN: 教晚间课程的那位物理学家自己编写了演示实验。
senses.why: Teaching is part of the profession, and the same title covers the classroom as well as the bench.
senses.whyCN: 教学是这一职业的一部分，因此同一个称谓既覆盖实验室工作台，也覆盖教室。

senses.title: The natural philosopher in older use
senses.definition: a person who studied nature before the modern disciplines separated, often called a philosopher of nature
senses.definitionCN: 在现代各学科分化之前研究自然的人，常被称为自然哲学家
senses.example: The physicist of that era also wrote on theology and optics.
senses.exampleCN: 那个时代的物理学家也写神学与光学方面的著作。
senses.why: The word arrived in the nineteenth century, and older figures are often given the title retrospectively even though they used a different one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在十九世纪才出现，较早的人物尽管自用别的称谓，仍常被追授这一称号。

senses.title: One who carries the method elsewhere
senses.titleCN: 把物理方法带到其他领域的人
senses.definition: a researcher trained in physics who applies its methods to biology, medicine, finance or computing
senses.definitionCN: 受过物理训练、却把其方法用于生物、医学、金融或计算领域的研究者
senses.example: The physicist now models how proteins fold.
senses.exampleCN: 这位物理学家现在为蛋白质折叠建立模型。
senses.why: A method travels with its practitioner, so the title can follow a person into a field that is not physics.
senses.whyCN: 方法随从业者一同迁移，因此这个称谓可以跟着一个人进入并非物理的领域。

senses.title: The writer who explains the subject
senses.titleCN: 面向公众解释物理的写作者
senses.definition: a person who makes the subject intelligible to non-specialists through books, lectures or broadcasts
senses.definitionCN: 通过书籍、讲座或广播使非专业者也能理解这门学科的人
senses.example: The physicist's popular books brought the subject to a wide audience.
senses.exampleCN: 这位物理学家的通俗著作把该学科带给了广大读者。
senses.why: When a field becomes specialised, someone must translate it outward, and the title follows that work too.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学科高度专门化，总得有人把它向外翻译，这个称谓也随这份工作延伸。

intro.en: Physicist is physics plus the Greek-derived suffix for a practitioner. The word was proposed in 1840 by William Whewell to distinguish a student of physics from a physician; that date is recorded rather than approximate.
intro.cn: physicist 由 physics 加希腊语来源的从业者后缀构成。这个词由威廉·休厄尔于 1840 年提出，用以把研究物理的人与医生区分开；这个年代是确切记载，而非约数。

items.en: Phusis 'nature' named the way things grow and behave on their own, and it is the ultimate root of the whole family.
items.cn: phusis 意为「自然」，指事物自行生长与表现的方式，是整个词族的最终词根。

items.en: Ta phusika 'natural things' was the title of Aristotle's treatises and became the name of the study of nature.
items.cn: ta phusika 意为「自然之物」，是亚里士多德诸篇的标题，后来成为研究自然的学问的名称。

items.en: Latin physica carried the subject into English, where the singular physic first meant medicine and the plural came to mean natural science.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physica 把这门学问带入英语；在英语中单数形式先指医学，复数形式后来指自然科学。

items.en: The suffix for a practitioner came through Latin and French; it marks a person devoted to a field, as in artist or chemist.
items.cn: 表示从业者的后缀经拉丁语与法语传入；它标示献身于某一领域的人，如艺术家或化学家。

items.en: William Whewell proposed physicist in 1840 for a student of physics, since physician already meant a healer. The date is recorded.
items.cn: 威廉·休厄尔在 1840 年提出用 physicist 指研究物理的人，因为 physician 已被医生占用。这个年代有确切记载。

items.en: As physics became a paid profession in universities and laboratories, the word settled into its present sense of a trained researcher or teacher.
items.cn: 随着物理学在大学与实验室中成为有薪职业，这个词稳定为现今「受过训练的研究者或教师」之义。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek word for nature or looks close to the title; the second group gives near alternatives for a person who studies the world.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语中表示「自然」的词，或与这个称谓形近；第二组是「研究世界的人」的近义替代。

entries.definition: A doctor of medicine; it comes from the same root but kept the older medical sense, which is why the two titles are constantly confused.
entries.definitionCN: 医生；它出自同一词根，却保留了较早的医学义，因此这两个称谓常被混淆。

entries.definition: The science of matter and motion; the entry word adds a suffix for the person, so one is the subject and the other the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质与运动的科学；本词加上表人的后缀，因此一个是学科，一个是从业者。

entries.definition: Of matter or the body; it describes things, while the entry word names a person.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的或身体的；它描述事物，而本词命名人。

entries.definition: The shape and strength of a body; it is close in spelling but names a frame, not a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的形态与力量；它拼写相近，却命名体格而不是职业。

entries.definition: Anyone who works in a systematic science; the entry word is one kind of scientist, defined by its field.
entries.definitionCN: 任何从事系统科学研究的人；本词是科学家的一种，由所属领域来界定。

entries.definition: A person who investigates a question systematically, in any field; it names the activity rather than the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 在任何领域系统探究某一问题的人；它命名活动，而不是学科。

entries.definition: The older name for a student of nature before disciplines separated; it is the historical counterpart of the entry word.
entries.definitionCN: 各学科分化之前研究自然者的旧称；它是本词在历史上的对应称谓。

entries.definition: A person devoted to one narrow area; it stresses depth in a corner rather than training in a whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻某一狭小领域的人；它强调在某个角落的深度，而不是对整个领域的训练。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek word for nature, the practitioner suffix, a recorded coinage and real branch titles.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊语中表示「自然」的词、表从业者的后缀、有确切记载的造词与真实的分支称谓。

normal.en: The word is the field plus a suffix for a person, so it always answers 'who works in physics'.
normal.cn: 这个词是学科名称加表人的后缀，因此它总是回答「谁在搞物理」。

normal.en: The family runs physics, physical, physically and astrophysics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括物理学、物理的、在物理上与天体物理。

normal.en: The recorded date is 1840, when the title was proposed to keep it apart from the word for a doctor.
normal.cn: 确切记载的年代是 1840 年，当时提出这个称谓是为了把它与表示医生的词分开。

normal.en: The title splits into theorist and experimentalist, and multiplies with branch prefixes.
normal.cn: 这个称谓分成理论者与实验者，并随分支前缀一同增殖。

normal.en: A method can travel, so a person trained in the field may end up modelling proteins or markets.
normal.cn: 方法可以迁移，因此受过该领域训练的人可能去为蛋白质或市场建模。

examples.en: The physicist argued that the anomaly was a fault in the detector.
examples.cn: 这位物理学家主张，那个异常是探测器的故障。

examples.en: Two physicists shared the prize for the same prediction.
examples.cn: 两位物理学家因同一项预言分享了该奖。

examples.en: As a physicist she was trained to distrust any number without an error bar.
examples.cn: 作为物理学家，她受过的训练让她不信任任何没有误差范围的数字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费兹希斯特」——先想「物理」，再想「人」：站在黑板前写公式、在台前测数据的那一位。

root: 希腊语 phusis「自然」→ phusika「自然之物」→ 拉丁语 physica「自然科学」→ 英语 physics；再加希腊语来源、经拉丁语与法语传入的从业者后缀 -ist，构成 physicist。该词由威廉·休厄尔于 1840 年提出，年代有确切记载。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings describe one person from different angles: the profession, the theorist and the experimentalist, the branch specialist and the one who carries the method elsewhere, the teacher and the popular writer, and the older natural philosopher whose title is applied retrospectively.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从不同角度描述同一种人：职业本身、理论者与实验者、分支专家与把方法带到别处的人、教师与通俗写作者，以及被追授旧称的自然哲学家。

branches.en: TEACHER AND WRITER: the classroom, and the translation of the field for the public.

senses.title: Existing in great number
senses.definition: is present in large numbers or amounts
senses.definitionCN: 以很大的数量或分量存在
senses.example: Fish were abundant in the clear lake.
senses.exampleCN: 清澈的湖里鱼很多。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to overflow, and plenty is the first thing overflow gives.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「溢出」，溢出首先带来的就是丰盛。

senses.title: Rich in a quality
senses.definition: contains a quality in large measure
senses.definitionCN: 大量含有某种特质
senses.example: The region is abundant in minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区矿产丰富。
senses.why: Overflow can be of anything, so the word also measures qualities.
senses.whyCN: 溢出之物可以是任何东西，因此这个词也用来衡量品质。

senses.title: More than enough
senses.definition: is more than enough for a need
senses.definitionCN: 超过所需，十分充足
senses.example: We had abundant time to prepare.
senses.exampleCN: 我们有充裕的时间做准备。
senses.why: A wave that spills over the rim is the image of surplus.
senses.whyCN: 漫过边缘的浪，正是「有余」的意象。

senses.title: Rich in words
senses.definition: in writing, is full and generous in expression
senses.definitionCN: 在写作中表达充分而丰沛
senses.example: Her abundant prose filled every page.
senses.exampleCN: 她丰沛的文笔写满了每一页。
senses.why: Language can overflow too, and the word describes a full style.
senses.whyCN: 语言也会溢出，这个词便用来形容饱满的文风。

senses.title: Generous in amount
senses.definition: is given in a generous quantity, as rain or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 如雨水或情感，给得十分大方
senses.example: Abundant rain saved the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 充沛的雨水挽救了收成。
senses.why: Nature's gifts that come in excess are called abundant.
senses.whyCN: 自然给的过多恩赐，就被称作 abundant。

senses.title: Growing thickly
senses.definition: of plants, grows thick and healthy
senses.definitionCN: 指植物长得茂密健壮
senses.example: Abundant grass covered the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 茂盛的草覆盖着山坡。
senses.why: A field that overflows with growth shows the same image.
senses.whyCN: 长满草木的田野呈现的是同一个意象。

senses.title: Full of life
senses.definition: in religious or poetic use, means full and rich in life
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教或诗意用法中，指生命充实丰盈
senses.example: They spoke of abundant life as a gift.
senses.exampleCN: 他们谈论丰盛的生命，视之为恩赐。
senses.why: Overflow becomes a metaphor for a life that lacks nothing.
senses.whyCN: 溢出成了「一无所缺的生活」的隐喻。

senses.title: An abundant number
senses.definition: in mathematics, is a number smaller than the sum of its divisors
senses.definitionCN: 数学上指小于其真因数之和的数
senses.example: Twelve is an abundant number.
senses.exampleCN: 十二是一个过剩数。
senses.why: The divisors add up beyond the number itself, an exact overflow.
senses.whyCN: 因数之和超过了这个数本身，正是一种精确的溢出。

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb meaning to overflow like water.
intro.cn: 这个词建在一个意为「像水一样溢出」的拉丁语动词上。

items.en: unda meant a wave or a stream of water.
items.cn: unda 意为波浪或水流。

items.en: abundare meant to overflow or run over like water.
items.cn: abundare 意为像水一样漫出、溢出。

items.en: abundans was its present participle, overflowing.
items.cn: abundans 是它的现在分词，意为「溢出的」。

items.en: the word passed into French as abundant, plentiful.
items.cn: 这个词以 abundant 的形式进入法语，意为充足。

items.en: English took abundant with the sense of plentiful.
items.cn: 英语借入 abundant，义为「丰富充足的」。

items.en: it now covers anything supplied in large measure.
items.cn: 如今它指任何供应充足的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group is the abundance family; the near-meaning group is other words for plenty.
note.cn: 形近组是 abundance 词族；近义组是别的表示「充足」的词。

normal.cn: unda 是拉丁语的「波浪」，正是词里的画面。

normal.cn: 前缀 ab- 带来「向外、越过」之意，浪便漫了出来。

normal.cn: 词尾 -ant 把拉丁分词变成形容词。

abstract.en: See a wave spilling over the rim of a full basin.
abstract.cn: 想象一盆水满到浪头漫过盆沿。

abstract.en: Picture branches bent low under heavy fruit.
abstract.cn: 想象枝条被沉甸甸的果子压弯。

abstract.en: Think of a table covered with more food than guests can eat.
abstract.cn: 想象一桌饭菜多到客人吃不完。

examples.en: The forest is abundant in wildlife.
examples.cn: 这片森林野生动物丰富。

examples.en: She found abundant evidence for her claim.
examples.cn: 她为自己的说法找到了大量证据。

examples.en: Water was abundant after the spring rains.
examples.cn: 春雨过后水源十分充足。

sensesIntro.en: Water running over its banks becomes plenty, richness in a quality, and finally a life that lacks nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: 水漫过堤岸，于是有了充足，有了品质上的丰盈，最后还有一无所缺的生命。

intro.cn: 这个词可拆成拉丁语前缀、词根与分词词尾。

latinIntro.cn: 词根 unda（波浪）也出现在 undulate（波动）里。

definition_en: in a way that makes a lot of loud sound, or with loud and insistent complaint
core_image: 声音挤出门缝，沿着走廊一路推过来
scene: 午休时间，走廊尽头那间教室的桌椅被推来推去，碰撞声一直传到办公室。 The boys were arguing noisily behind the closed door.
sceneCN: 这里 noisily 是「吵闹地、大声地」（第 1 个义项：以很大的声音做事）；句意为男孩们在关着的门后大声争吵。图中可辨识物件：被推动的课桌、走廊尽头关着的门、办公室的窗户。

senses.title: In a loud and disturbing way
senses.definition: with a lot of loud sound that disturbs the people around
senses.definitionCN: 发出很大的声响，打扰到周围的人
senses.example: The children played noisily in the yard until dark.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在院子里吵闹地玩到天黑。
senses.why: The adverb takes the adjective noisy and adds -ly, so the sound leaves the object and becomes the manner of an action.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由形容词 noisy 加 -ly 构成，于是声音从物体身上离开，变成做一件事的方式。

senses.title: With loud complaint or protest
senses.definition: with loud and insistent complaint, so that everyone nearby can hear it
senses.definitionCN: 以响亮而执拗的抱怨表达不满，让附近的人都听得见
senses.example: The crowd protested noisily outside the town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 人群在市政厅外大声抗议。
senses.why: When a group wants to be heard, volume becomes a tool of pressure, and the same manner word shifts from mere sound to public demand.
senses.whyCN: 当一个群体希望被听见时，音量就成了施压的工具；同一个方式副词于是从单纯的声音转向公开的诉求。

senses.title: With much clatter from things or machines
senses.definition: with a continuous clatter or rattle, usually made by machines or objects rather than by people
senses.definitionCN: 伴随着持续的碰撞声或咔嗒声，通常来自机器或物件而不是人
senses.example: The old printer ran noisily all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧打印机整夜响个不停。
senses.why: Objects make noise without intending anything, so the adverb can simply name the clatter that comes along with their working.
senses.whyCN: 物件本身并无意图，却照样发出声响，所以这个副词也能单纯描述它们运转时伴随的嘈杂。

intro.en: Noisily is the adjective noisy plus the adverb ending -ly; the deeper origin of noise is uncertain, and one common suggestion links it to Latin nausea through Old French.
intro.cn: noisily 是形容词 noisy 加副词词尾 -ly；noise 更早的来源不确定，一种常见的说法认为它经古法语与拉丁语 nausea 有关。

items.en: The ultimate source of noise is uncertain; dictionaries often record a suggested link with Latin nausea, but that link is not proved.
items.cn: noise 的最终来源不确定；词典常记下一种与拉丁语 nausea 相关的猜测，但这条线索并未得到证实。

items.en: Old French noise meant quarrel, outcry or din, and it could name a loud dispute as well as a loud sound.
items.cn: 古法语 noise 意为争吵、喊叫、喧闹，既可指大声的争执，也可指响亮的声响。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word for a loud outcry or a confusing din before it settled as the general term for unwanted sound.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个词，先指大声喊叫或杂乱的喧闹，后来才固定为「不受欢迎的声音」的通用说法。

items.en: The adjective noisy was formed with -y, and the adverb noisily followed with -ly.
items.cn: 形容词 noisy 由 -y 构成，副词 noisily 随后由 -ly 构成。

items.en: Modern English uses noisily for the manner of an action, especially play, speech and machines.
items.cn: 现代英语用 noisily 描述动作的方式，尤其见于玩耍、说话和机器运转。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noise family and its endings; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs of loud or overwhelming sound.
note.cn: 形近组收 noise 词族及其词尾形式；近义组收其他表示响亮或压倒性声音的副词。

entries.definitionCN: 发出或充满响亮声音的；这个副词背后的形容词。

entries.definitionCN: 以很大的音量；表示音量大的一般副词。

entries.definition: With rough, disorderly and noisy behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 以粗野、混乱而吵闹的方式。

entries.definition: So loudly that it seems to block out all other sound.
entries.definitionCN: 响得几乎把其他声音都盖住。

entries.definition: With a loud and continuous demand or outcry.
entries.definitionCN: 以响亮而持续的要求或呼喊。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from noise through two endings, and its family keeps turning sound into a quality and then into a manner of acting.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由 noise 经两个词尾层层构成；词族不断把声音变成性质，再变成做事的方式。

normal.en: Noise plus -y gives noisy, and noisy plus -ly gives noisily.
normal.cn: noise 加 -y 得 noisy，noisy 再加 -ly 得 noisily。

normal.en: The y at the end of noisy turns into i before -ly: noisily, not noisyly.
normal.cn: noisy 末尾的 y 在 -ly 前变为 i：写作 noisily，不是 noisyly。

normal.en: Noisy sits before a noun, while noisily sits beside a verb and tells how it is done.
normal.cn: noisy 放在名词前，noisily 则靠近动词，说明动作是怎么做的。

normal.en: The comparative uses more and most, never noisilier.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more 与 most，不说 noisilier。

normal.en: The noun behind the whole family is noise, an uncountable word for unwanted sound.
normal.cn: 整个词族背后的名词是 noise，用来指不受欢迎的声音，通常不可数。

abstract.en: A sound becomes a habit of a place, then a quality of a thing, then a way of acting.
abstract.cn: 一种声音先变成一个地方的习惯，再变成事物的性质，最后变成做事的方式。

abstract.en: The same adverb covers children at play and a crowd demanding to be heard, because volume is both joy and pressure.
abstract.cn: 同一个副词既描述玩耍的孩子，也描述要求被听见的人群，因为音量既是快乐，也是压力。

abstract.en: Noisily is what a room sounds like when nobody inside remembers that others are near.
abstract.cn: noisily 是一间屋子里的人忘了隔壁还有别人时，那间屋子听起来的样子。

senses.title: Relating to light
senses.definition: concerned with light itself, its production, transmission or detection
senses.definitionCN: 涉及光本身，即其产生、传播或探测
senses.example: The optical fibre carries the signal as pulses of light along a glass thread.
senses.exampleCN: 光纤把信号以光脉冲形式沿玻璃丝传送。
senses.why: Greek optikos meant of sight, from optos, seen; the adjective moved from the eye to the light the eye uses.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 optikos 意为「视觉的」，出自 optos「被看见的」；这个形容词从眼睛移到了眼睛所用的光。

senses.title: An optical instrument
senses.titleCN: 使用透镜或反射镜的光学仪器
senses.definition: describing a device that uses lenses, mirrors or prisms to form an image or direct light
senses.definitionCN: 描述用透镜、反射镜或棱镜成像或导光的装置
senses.example: The laboratory keeps its optical instruments in a dust-free cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把光学仪器放在无尘柜里。
senses.why: the adjective names the working principle rather than the purpose, so a microscope and a camera share it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词命名的是工作原理而非用途，因此显微镜与相机共用它。

senses.title: An optical illusion
senses.titleCN: 视错觉：眼睛被图案骗过
senses.definition: a false perception produced when the visual system interprets a pattern in the wrong way
senses.definitionCN: 视觉系统对图案作出错误解释时产生的错误感知
senses.example: The optical illusion made the straight lines appear to bend.
senses.exampleCN: 这个视错觉让直线看起来弯了。
senses.why: the error lies in sight rather than in light, which is why the word keeps its link to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 错误出在视觉而非光线，因此这个词仍与眼睛相连。

senses.title: An optical fibre
senses.titleCN: 光纤：把光约束在细丝中传输
senses.definition: a thin thread of glass that guides light by repeated internal reflection, used to carry signals
senses.definitionCN: 靠反复全反射把光约束其中的细玻璃丝，用于传输信号
senses.example: Optical fibre replaced copper in the new trunk line.
senses.exampleCN: 新干线路上，光纤取代了铜线。
senses.why: the fibre works by optics alone, so the adjective distinguishes it from the electrical cable it replaced.
senses.whyCN: 这种纤维只靠光学工作，因此用该形容词与它取代的电线区分开来。

senses.title: The optical axis
senses.titleCN: 光轴：光学系统的对称中心线
senses.definition: the line through the centre of a lens or mirror system about which the optical elements are arranged
senses.definitionCN: 穿过透镜或反射镜系统中心、各光学元件据以排列的那条线
senses.example: The lens was mounted slightly off the optical axis.
senses.exampleCN: 这片透镜安装得略微偏离光轴。
senses.why: a system needs a reference line, and the adjective marks that the line belongs to light rather than to mechanics.
senses.whyCN: 系统需要一条参考线，这个形容词标出这条线属于光而非机械。

senses.title: Optical character recognition
senses.titleCN: 光学字符识别：让机器读印刷文字
senses.definition: the automatic conversion of a picture of printed text into machine-readable characters
senses.definitionCN: 把印刷文字的图像自动转成机器可读字符
senses.example: Optical character recognition turned the scanned page into searchable text.
senses.exampleCN: 光学字符识别把扫描页变成了可检索的文本。
senses.why: the machine looks at the page with light and lenses, so computing borrowed the adjective for the seeing part.
senses.whyCN: 机器用光与镜头看这一页，因此计算机领域借这个形容词指「看」的那一环。

senses.title: Optical astronomy
senses.titleCN: 光学天文学：用可见光观测
senses.definition: the branch of astronomy that observes visible light rather than radio, infrared or other bands
senses.definitionCN: 观测可见光而非射电、红外等波段的天文学分支
senses.example: Optical astronomy still supplies the sharpest pictures of planets.
senses.exampleCN: 光学天文学仍能提供最清晰的行星图像。
senses.why: as other bands opened up, the old visible-light work needed a label, and optical became it.
senses.whyCN: 当别的波段被打开后，旧的可见光工作需要一个标签，optical 便承担了这个角色。

senses.title: Abstract: visual rather than conceptual
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：视觉层面的，而非概念层面的
senses.definition: concerned with how something looks to the eye rather than with what it means
senses.definitionCN: 关注某物在眼睛看来是什么样，而非它意味着什么
senses.example: The disagreement was optical rather than substantive, a matter of layout.
senses.exampleCN: 这一分歧是视觉层面的而非实质性的，只是版式问题。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the channel: something is judged by appearance, not by content.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留通道：判断依据是外观，而非内容。

intro.en: Optical comes through Latin opticus from Greek optikos, of sight, built on optos, seen, from the verb for seeing. The word entered English in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: optical 经拉丁 opticus 来自希腊 optikos「视觉的」，其词为 optos「被看见的」，出自「看见」这一动词。这个词在十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: Ops meant the eye or the face, and the related verb meant to see; the family also gives optos, seen.
items.cn: ops 指眼睛或脸，相关动词意为「看见」；这一族还给出 optos「被看见的」。

items.en: Optikos meant of sight or of the science of seeing, and it named the study of light and vision.
items.cn: optikos 意为「视觉的、看之学的」，并用来说明研究光与视觉的学问。

items.en: Latin took the adjective as opticus; English optical follows the Latin stem with the suffix -al.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 opticus；英语 optical 沿用拉丁词干并加后缀 -al。

items.en: English optical appears in the sixteenth century, first in treatises on lenses and the eye.
items.cn: 英语 optical 出现于十六世纪，最初见于论透镜与眼睛的著作。

items.en: Optical fibre, optical character recognition and optical astronomy are all twentieth-century compounds built on the adjective.
items.cn: 光纤、光学字符识别与光学天文学都是 20 世纪以该形容词构成的复合词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root only): the further origin of Greek ops is unsettled, and the link sometimes drawn to a Indo-European seeing root is a reconstruction rather than a demonstrated step.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词根）：希腊 ops 的更早来源没有定论，有人把它与某个印欧「看见」词根相连，那属重构，而非已证实的环节。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like optical but come from different roots or different word classes; group two holds the adjectives that also describe sight and light.
note.cn: 第一组是与 optical 形近、却来自不同词根或不同词类的词；第二组是同样描述视觉与光的形容词。

entries.definition: The science of light, a plural-looking singular noun; it is the discipline, not a property of an object.
entries.definitionCN: 研究光的学科，形式是复数而作单数用；它是学科，不是物体的属性。

entries.definition: A person who makes or sells lenses and spectacles, built with -ian marking a practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或售卖镜片与眼镜的人，后缀 -ian 表示从业者。

entries.definition: From optio, a choice, not from ops, the eye; it means not compulsory and has no optical sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 optio「选择」，而非 ops「眼睛」；意为「非必需的」，完全没有光学含义。

entries.definition: The profession of measuring vision and prescribing lenses, from optos plus metron, measure.
entries.definitionCN: 测量视力并验配镜片的行业，由 optos 加 metron「测量」构成。

entries.definition: Relating to the act of seeing or to visual perception, as in visual memory.
entries.definitionCN: 与看这一行为或视觉感知有关，如视觉记忆。

entries.definition: Relating to the eye as an organ, as in ocular muscles; it is anatomical rather than physical.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为器官的眼睛有关，如眼肌；属解剖用语而非物理用语。

entries.definition: Relating to light as a stimulus to living things, as in the photic zone of the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 与光作为生物刺激有关，如海洋透光层。

entries.definition: A plain descriptive phrase for equipment built around lenses; it lacks the scientific scope of optical.
entries.definitionCN: 对围绕透镜构造的设备的朴素描述，缺少 optical 的科学涵盖面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root, the real word family and the real twentieth-century compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、真实的词族与真实的 20 世纪复合词。

normal.en: Greek optos means seen, so optical is about what light makes visible.
normal.cn: 希腊 optos 意为「被看见的」，因此 optical 讲的是光使什么可见。

normal.en: Optics is the field, an optician is the person, and optically is the adverb.
normal.cn: optics 是学科，optician 是从业者，optically 是副词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: optical fibre, optical illusion, optical axis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：光纤、视错觉、光轴。

normal.en: Optical astronomy means visible-light astronomy, as opposed to radio astronomy.
normal.cn: 「光学天文学」指依靠可见光的观测分支，与射电天文学相对。

normal.en: Optional looks similar but comes from choice, not from the eye.
normal.cn: optional 形近，却出自「选择」而非「眼睛」。

abstract.en: Picture a thread of glass so clear that only the light inside it shows the way.
abstract.cn: 想象一根玻璃丝清透到只有里面的光能指路。

abstract.en: Picture two parallel lines that insist on looking bent.
abstract.cn: 想象两条平行线偏要看起来是弯的。

abstract.en: Picture a page that a machine reads with a lamp instead of a mind.
abstract.cn: 想象机器用一盏灯而不是用头脑去读的一页纸。

examples.en: The telescope is the oldest optical instrument still in daily use.
examples.cn: 望远镜是仍被日常使用的最古老光学仪器。

examples.en: Optical fibres carry most of the world long-distance data traffic.
examples.cn: 光纤承载了世界上大部分长途数据流量。

examples.en: The museum uses optical character recognition to index its labels.
examples.cn: 博物馆用光学字符识别为标签建索引。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「opt（看）+ ical」——与看、与光有关的 → 光学的；用镜片和光工作的 → 光学仪器

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with light itself, then pass through instruments, illusions, fibres, axes, machine reading and astronomy, and end as a figure for appearance over substance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从光本身开始，随后经过仪器、错觉、光纤、光轴、机器识读与天文，最后成为「外观压过实质」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass thread guiding pulses of light to a small bright point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根玻璃丝把光脉冲引到一个小小的亮点。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL CORE: light produced, transmitted or detected is the trunk of every other sense.
branches.cn: 物理核心：光的产生、传播或探测，是其余义项的树干。

branches.en: HARDWARE: instruments and axes are arranged around the behaviour of light.
branches.cn: 硬件：仪器与光轴都围绕光的行为了布置。

branches.en: THE EYE FAILS: an illusion is an error of sight, not of light.
branches.cn: 眼睛出错：错觉是视觉的错误，而非光的错误。

branches.en: APPLICATIONS: fibre, character recognition and optical astronomy each take one technical face of light.
branches.cn: 应用：光纤、字符识别与光学天文，各取光的某一个技术侧面。

branches.en: APPEARANCE: what is judged is how it looks, not what it is.
branches.cn: 外观：被判断的是它看起来怎样，而不是它是什么。

intro.en: Optical is a Greek adjective that reached English through Latin, and its stem also builds the names of the field and the practitioner.
intro.cn: optical 是经拉丁进入英语的希腊形容词，其词干还构成学科名与从业者名。

latinIntro.en: Greek optikos became Latin opticus; English added -al. The noun optics keeps the Greek plural ending -ics that marks a field.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 optikos 转为拉丁 opticus，英语再加 -al。名词 optics 保留希腊复数后缀 -ics，用来表示学科。

definition_zh: 使习惯；使适应
definition_en: to make yourself or someone else familiar with something through repeated experience
core_image: 每天走同一条石子路，脚底慢慢不再觉得硌
scene: 刚到城里时，她逼自己适应夜里的车声。 She accustomed herself to the noise of the city.
sceneCN: 这里的 accustom 是「使自己习惯」（第 1 个义项：主动去适应）；句意是她让自己习惯了城里的噪声。

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转化而来，义为「习惯的；惯常的」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不习惯的」

senses.title: To make used to something
senses.definition: to train a person or an animal to accept a new condition
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复接触，让人或动物接受新的状况
senses.example: The coach accustomed the team to early training.
senses.exampleCN: 教练让队伍习惯了清早训练。
senses.why: The Old French base costume means habitual practice, so the verb is literally to turn something into a habit.
senses.whyCN: 古法语词基 costume 意为「惯常的做法」，所以这个词字面上就是「把某事变成习惯」。

senses.title: To be in the habit of
senses.definition: to have become familiar with something, usually in the phrase be accustomed to
senses.definitionCN: 已经对某事熟悉，常用于 be accustomed to 这一说法
senses.example: They are accustomed to long walks in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 他们习惯了在雨里长途步行。
senses.why: Once the training is complete, the verb's participle freezes into a state adjective: not the act of training but the settled habit.
senses.whyCN: 训练一旦完成，动词的分词就凝固成状态形容词：说的不再是训练的动作，而是安顿下来的习惯。

intro.en: The word comes through Old French, from a Latin noun for habitual practice.
intro.cn: 这个词经由古法语而来，源头是拉丁语中表示「惯常做法」的名词。

items.en: consuetudo meant custom, habit or familiar practice.
items.cn: consuetudo 意为习俗、习惯或惯常做法。

items.en: costume meant a usual manner or practice.
items.cn: 古法语 costume 意为惯常的方式或做法。

items.en: acostumer meant to make something habitual.
items.cn: acostumer 意为使某事成为习惯。

items.en: accustom entered English as a verb of training and use.
items.cn: accustom 在十五世纪进入英语，是表示训练与习惯的动词。

note.en: The first group is the custom family; the second is other verbs of getting used.

senses.title: As was long accepted to be so
senses.definition: used to state what has long been believed or assumed, often before a correction
senses.definitionCN: 用于陈述长久以来的看法或假定，后面常跟一个纠正
senses.example: Traditionally, the work was thought to be men's work.
senses.exampleCN: 传统上，这项工作被认为是男人的活。
senses.why: Attitudes are inherited as well as actions, so the adverb also frames an old belief as an old belief.
senses.whyCN: 被传下来的除了做法还有看法，所以这个副词也用来把一种旧看法框定为「旧看法」。

senses.title: In the usual or expected place
senses.definition: in the position or role that has become the pattern, especially in a family or team
senses.definitionCN: 在已成定式的位置或角色上，尤指家庭或团队中
senses.example: Traditionally, the youngest child sits nearest the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 按惯例，最小的孩子坐在离火最近的地方。
senses.why: Small pattern-making habits repeat until they become the expected arrangement, and the adverb marks them as such.
senses.whyCN: 小习惯不断重复，直到成为众人预期的安排，副词就标记这种安排。

senses.title: By the older method rather than the new
senses.definition: used before a participle to say that something is done with the older, non-modern technique
senses.definitionCN: 用在分词前，表示采用较古老而非现代的技术来做
senses.example: The cheese is traditionally made with raw milk.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪传统上用生奶制作。
senses.why: When two methods exist, the older one needs a label, and this adverb supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 当两种方法并存，较旧的那一种需要一个标签，而这个副词正好提供它。

senses.title: According to long-standing practice in a field
senses.definition: used to describe what a subject or profession has done by established practice
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述某个学科或行业按既定做法所做的事
senses.example: The subject is traditionally divided into three periods.
senses.exampleCN: 这门学科传统上分为三个时期。
senses.why: Every field carries fixed divisions, so the adverb marks what the old division has always been.
senses.whyCN: 每门学科都带着固定的划分，副词就标记这种旧划分一直是怎样。

intro.en: Traditionally is tradition with the adjective ending -al and the adverb ending -ly, whose root is Latin tradere, to hand over.
intro.cn: traditionally 是 tradition 加形容词词尾 -al 与副词词尾 -ly，其词根是拉丁语 tradere（交付）。

items.en: Traditio is a delivery or handover, built from trans-, across, and dare, to give.
items.cn: traditio 意为交付、递交，由 trans-（穿过）与 dare（给）构成。

items.en: Tradition enters English through Old French, and the adjective traditional is formed in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: tradition 经古法语进入英语，形容词 traditional 在十六世纪形成。

items.en: The adverb ending -ly is added to many such adjectives in the seventeenth century, giving traditionally.
items.cn: 十七世纪，许多同类形容词加上副词词尾 -ly，traditionally 由此成形。

items.en: The adverb becomes frequent in writing about food, farming, and institutions from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，这个副词在关于饮食、农业与机构的写作中频繁出现。

items.en: In modern usage it often frames a claim before the writer disagrees with it.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，它常常出现在作者即将表示异议之前，为旧说法作框。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the -al and -ly chain of the family, while the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for usual and older practice.
note.cn: 形近组顺着这一族 -al 与 -ly 的链条展开，近义组收集表示惯常与较旧做法的副词。

entries.definition: following old custom
a custom handed down
a person who defends old customs
in a way relating to change
entries.definitionCN: 过渡地，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: according to habit or custom
in the accepted way
most of the time

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the -al plus -ly chain, from the passive constructions the adverb prefers, and from the picture of the old path.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从 -al 加 -ly 的链条、这个副词偏爱的被动结构以及老路的画面入手。

normal.en: Tradition, traditional, traditionally: noun, adjective, adverb, one step each.
normal.cn: tradition、traditional、traditionally，名词、形容词、副词，各一步。

normal.en: Traditionally made, traditionally grown, traditionally cooked: the word loves a passive participle.
normal.cn: traditionally made、traditionally grown、traditionally cooked，这个词最爱跟被动分词。

normal.en: Traditionally, the work was thought to be men's work: the adverb sets an old belief up for review.
normal.cn: 这个副词先把「这项工作一向被认为是男人的活」这样的旧看法摆出来等评断。

normal.en: The -ally ending is -al plus -ly, never a single suffix.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ally 是 -al 加 -ly，从来不是一个后缀。

normal.en: If the adverb sits first with a comma, it usually frames a whole old custom.
normal.cn: 若副词位于句首并带逗号，通常是为一整套旧习俗作框。

abstract.en: Picture feet that turn at a certain corner without anyone telling them to.
abstract.cn: 想象一些脚在某个转角自动拐弯，没人指挥。

abstract.en: Think of a recipe that never says why, only how.
abstract.cn: 想一份从不解释为什么、只说怎么做的菜谱。

abstract.en: Traditionally is the voice of the path, not of the planner.
abstract.cn: traditionally 是路径自己的声音，而不是规划者的声音。

examples.en: This cheese is traditionally made in small mountain farms.
examples.cn: 这种奶酪传统上在小山场里制作。

examples.en: Traditionally, the eldest son inherits the house.
examples.cn: 传统上，长子继承这所房子。

examples.en: The festival is traditionally held in early spring.
examples.cn: 这个节日传统上在早春举行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿递神呢里」——在穿递下来的神气东西里面，照老规矩办。

root: 拉丁语 tradere（交付）→ traditio（传承）→ 英语 tradition → traditional（+ -al）→ traditionally（+ -ly）。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb begins as a plain report of doing things the old way, then covers old beliefs, expected arrangements, older techniques, and the fixed divisions of a subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词起初只是平实报告「照老办法做」，之后涵盖旧看法、预期中的安排、较旧的技术，以及一门学科的固定划分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steps that follow a path worn by many previous walkers.
core.cn: 核心意象：跟着众多前人踩出的路走的脚步。

branches.en: The plain report of customary action.
branches.cn: 对惯常做法的平实陈述。

branches.en: The framing of an inherited belief.
branches.cn: 为承袭来的看法作框。

branches.en: The expected family or team arrangement.
branches.cn: 家庭或团队中预期的安排。

branches.en: The older technique beside the new one.
branches.cn: 与新技术并存的旧技术。

branches.en: The fixed divisions of a subject.
branches.cn: 一门学科的固定划分。

intro.en: The word stacks the Latin noun ending -tion, the adjective suffix -al, and the English adverb suffix -ly on the giving root.
intro.cn: 本词在「给」的词根上依次叠加拉丁名词词尾 -tion、形容词后缀 -al 与英语副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The Latin giving verb and the handover noun behind the whole stack are listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 下面列出这一整串叠加背后的拉丁语「给」动词与「交付」名词。

items.example: Dare is the root of the whole chain.
The prefix makes the giving a handover.
Tradition is the act of handing down.
The -ly ending turns the adjective into an adverb.

items.meaningCN: 由 -al 与 -ly 合成的拼写
items.exampleCN: 拼写 -ally 显示出两个后缀。

items.example: Traditionalism is the belief, not the manner.
A traditionalist acts from the belief.

definition_zh: 小木屋；船舱；机舱
definition_en: a small simple house made of wood
core_image: 林间用原木搭起的小屋
scene: 雪落在松林深处。 They stayed in a wooden cabin for the night.
sceneCN: 这里 cabin 是「小木屋」（第 1 个义项：简陋的木制小屋）；句意是他们在一间木屋里过夜。

derivatives.zh: 被关在小空间里的，受限制的
村舍，语义相关的小屋
简陋小屋，语义相关

senses.title: A small wooden house
senses.definition: a simple house built of wood, often in the country
senses.definitionCN: 用木头搭成的简陋房屋，常在乡间
senses.example: They stayed in a wooden cabin for the night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一间木屋里过夜。
senses.why: The core image is a small shelter raised from rough logs.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是用粗糙原木搭起的小小栖身处。

senses.title: A room on a ship
senses.definition: a small private room on a ship for passengers
senses.definitionCN: 船上供乘客使用的小舱室
senses.example: Their cabin looked out over the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的船舱朝海。
senses.why: A small enclosed space on a ship repeats the snug shelter of the wooden house.
senses.whyCN: 船上狭小的封闭空间，沿用了木屋那种紧凑的庇护感。

senses.title: The passenger area of a plane
senses.definition: the part of an aircraft where passengers sit
senses.definitionCN: 飞机上乘客乘坐的部分
senses.example: The cabin lights dimmed before take-off.
senses.exampleCN: 起飞前机舱的灯暗了下来。
senses.why: The enclosed passenger space of an aircraft took the same word.
senses.whyCN: 飞机上封闭的乘客空间，也沿用了同一个词。

intro.en: Cabin comes from French and Latin words for a small hut.
intro.cn: cabin 来自法语与拉丁语中表示小屋的词。

items.en: capanna meant a simple hut or stall.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capanna 指简陋的小屋或棚子。

items.en: cabane named a small dwelling.
items.cn: 古法语 cabane 指小型住所。

items.en: cabin named a rough shelter and a ship room.
items.cn: 中古英语 cabin 兼指简陋住所与船上舱室。

items.en: Log cabins became a symbol of frontier life.
items.cn: 十九世纪原木小屋成为拓荒生活的象征。

items.en: Cabin covers wooden houses, ship rooms and aircraft cabins.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cabin 兼指木屋、船舱与机舱。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cabin base; the near-meaning group gives other small dwellings.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cabin 词基；近义组是其他小屋类住所。

entries.definition: a small shelter by a pool or beach
entries.definitionCN: 泳池或海滩边的小棚屋，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: confined in a small space
a piece of storage furniture
entries.definitionCN: 储物橱柜，与 cabin 同源

entries.definition: a small house in the country
a very simple small shelter
a small house used for holidays or hunting

normalIntro.en: Cabin names a small enclosed shelter on land, sea or in the air.
normalIntro.cn: cabin 指陆上、海上或空中一个狭小的封闭空间。

normal.en: The plural is cabins.
normal.cn: 复数是 cabins。

normal.en: A log cabin is built from whole logs.
normal.cn: log cabin 用整根原木搭建。

normal.en: Cabin crew work in the passenger cabin.
normal.cn: cabin crew 在客舱工作。

normal.en: On a ship you book a cabin.
normal.cn: 在船上要预订船舱。

normal.en: The word shares a root with cabinet.
normal.cn: 这个词与 cabinet 同源。

abstract.en: See lamplight in a small window among pines.
abstract.cn: 想象松林中一扇小窗透出灯光。

abstract.en: See a narrow bunk rocking with the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象窄窄的床铺随海浪摇晃。

abstract.en: See the cabin lights dim as the plane taxis.
abstract.cn: 想象飞机滑行时机舱灯变暗。

examples.en: They stayed in a wooden cabin for the night.
examples.cn: 他们在一间木屋里过夜。

examples.en: Their cabin looked out over the sea.
examples.cn: 他们的船舱朝海。

examples.en: The cabin lights dimmed before take-off.
examples.cn: 起飞前机舱的灯暗了下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: cab 是出租车，in 是里面，合起来像钻进一辆小小的车厢，再变成林子里的小屋和船上的舱室。

root: cabin 经古法语 cabane 上溯到拉丁语 capanna，本指简陋的小屋或棚子，后来用于船上的舱室与飞机的客舱。

sensesIntro.en: A wooden house, a ship room and an aircraft passenger area.
sensesIntro.cn: 木屋、船上舱室，以及飞机客舱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small log shelter in the woods.
core.cn: 核心意象：林中一间原木小屋。

branches.en: a log cabin
branches.cn: 原木小屋

branches.en: a cabin in the woods
branches.cn: 林中木屋

branches.en: book a cabin
branches.cn: 预订船舱

branches.en: a private cabin
branches.cn: 私人舱室

branches.en: the passenger cabin
branches.cn: 客舱

intro.en: Cabin forms compounds with crew and takes the ending -ed.
intro.cn: cabin 能与 crew 组成复合词，也能加 -ed 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin capanna, a hut.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 capanna，意为小屋。

definition_zh: 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；蓬勃发展
definition_en: to grow well and be healthy, or to be successful and continue growing strongly
core_image: 窗台上一盆绿植越过花盆边缘，越窜越高
scene: 小区角落原本光秃的墙根,如今爬山虎长得密密匝匝。 The old brick wall is now covered with ivy that thrives in the damp shade.
sceneCN: 这里 thrive 是「茁壮成长」（第 2 个义项：植物长得旺盛）；句意为那面旧砖墙如今爬满了在潮湿阴处长得旺盛的常春藤。

collocations.zh: 在压力下反而表现出色

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「兴旺的；繁荣的」
本词的过去分词形式，义为「已兴旺起来」
与本词同源的近亲名词，义为「节俭」（语义已分化）

senses.title: To succeed and grow strong
senses.definition: to become successful, strong and healthy, of a business, city or person
senses.definitionCN: 指事业、城市或人变得成功、强健、健康
senses.example: The little bookshop thrived after it began hosting readings.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小书店开始办朗读会之后兴旺起来。
senses.why: The Norse verb meant to take a firm hold, so success is pictured as a grip that holds.
senses.whyCN: 这个北欧语动词意为「牢牢抓住」，因此成功被想象成一把抓稳的手。

senses.title: To grow vigorously, of plants
senses.definition: to grow strongly and healthily, especially of plants in favourable conditions
senses.definitionCN: 尤指植物在适宜条件下长得健壮旺盛
senses.example: These roses thrive in full sun and well-drained soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这些玫瑰在阳光充足、排水良好的土里长得很好。
senses.why: Applied to plants, the grip image becomes roots holding soil and shoots pushing up.
senses.whyCN: 用在植物上，抓握的意象就变成根系抓住土壤、枝条向上推送。

senses.title: To do well in difficult conditions
senses.definition: to do well because of conditions that would weaken others, used with on or under
senses.definitionCN: 因那些会削弱别人的条件而表现得更好，后接 on 或 under
senses.example: Some people thrive on a tight deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人在紧迫的期限下反而状态极好。
senses.why: The preposition on marks the source: the pressure itself feeds the growth.
senses.whyCN: 介词 on 标出源头：压力本身成了生长的养分。

senses.title: To flourish culturally or socially
senses.definition: to develop strongly and spread, of ideas, arts or customs
senses.definitionCN: 指观念、艺术或习俗发展壮大并传播开来
senses.example: Coffee culture thrives in this part of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡文化在城市的这一带很盛行。
senses.why: Ideas are treated like plants: they take hold, spread and bloom across a place.
senses.whyCN: 观念被当作植物看待：它们落地、蔓延，在一个地方成片开花。

intro.en: Thrive comes from Old Norse, and its older meaning was to grasp or to seize, not to grow.
intro.cn: thrive 来自古北欧语，较早的意义是「抓住」，并非「成长」。

items.en: The Norse verb þrífask meant to prosper and also to grasp or take hold of something.
items.cn: 北欧语动词 þrífask 既表示「兴旺」，也表示「抓住、握住」。

items.en: The root behind it meant to grip or to press, the same pressure family that gives threat.
items.cn: 其背后的词根意为「抓紧、压住」，与 threat 同属压迫一族。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word from Norse settlers and used it for growing strong and prospering.
items.cn: 中古英语从北欧移民借入这个词，用来表示「长得强健」与「兴旺」。

items.en: Early modern English gave the word both a bodily and a commercial sense, a thriving plant and a thriving trade.
items.cn: 早期现代英语让它兼具身体与商业两面：茁壮的植物与兴隆的生意。

items.en: Modern English added the pattern thrive on, meaning to do better because of something.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出 thrive on 的用法，表示「因某事而更好」。

note.en: The first group gathers the thrive family and its Norse relatives; the second compares words of success and growth.
note.cn: 第一组收 thrive 词族及其北欧近亲；第二组比较表示成功与生长的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a healthy, growing business or plant.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「兴旺的、繁荣的」

entries.definition: From the same Norse family, meaning careful management of money.
entries.definitionCN: 节俭（同源，语义已转向理财）

entries.definition: The adjective of thrift, meaning careful with money.
Very exciting; the -ill- pattern is close but the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 令人激动的（-ill- 拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: To grow or develop very well, especially of plants and arts.
entries.definitionCN: 繁荣；茂盛（尤指植物与艺术）

entries.definition: To become successful, usually of money and business.
entries.definitionCN: 兴旺；致富（多指经济层面）

entries.definition: To open into flower, and figuratively to come into your own.
To dry up and fade, the exact opposite of thriving.

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the Norse origin, the grip image, and the thrive on pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自北欧来源、「抓握」意象，以及 thrive on 句式。

normal.en: The old Norse verb meant to grab hold, and a plant that thrives has taken firm hold of its soil.
normal.cn: 古北欧语动词意为「抓住」，长得旺的植物正是抓住了土。

normal.en: Thrive on shows the pattern: the thing that would hurt others helps you.
normal.cn: thrive on 显示这种句式：会让别人受伤的东西反而帮了你。

normal.en: The past tense form throve is old style, and thrived is the everyday choice.
normal.cn: 过去式 throve 偏古，日常多用 thrived。

normal.en: Thrift comes from the same Norse family: both words are about making something go far.
normal.cn: thrift 出自同一条北欧语脉：两个词都关乎「让有限之物发挥到极致」。

normal.en: A thriving market and a thriving rose bush share one word.
normal.cn: 繁荣的市场与旺盛的玫瑰丛共用一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a vine that has found the one crack of light and climbed over the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一株藤找到了唯一的裂缝阳光，一路爬过墙头。

abstract.en: To thrive is not just to survive the winter but to burst out in spring.
abstract.cn: thrive 不只是熬过冬天，而是春天炸开般地生长。

abstract.en: The word makes growth look like a grip that keeps getting tighter.
abstract.cn: 这个词让成长看起来像一把越握越紧的手。

examples.en: Small firms thrive when rules are simple.
examples.cn: 规则简单时，小公司就能兴旺。

examples.en: These plants thrive in damp, shaded corners.
examples.cn: 这些植物在阴湿的角落里长得很好。

examples.en: She thrives on difficult problems.
examples.cn: 她越遇到难题越有劲头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹五」——一脚踹开五道门槛，生意越踹越旺 → thrive 兴旺

root: 古北欧语 þrífask「兴旺；抓住」，与日耳曼语「抓紧、压住」词根同源（与 threat 同族）；中古英语借入后表示「长壮、兴旺」，现代又发展出 thrive on 的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Thrive keeps one image of taking a firm hold and lets it grow into business success, healthy plants, strength under pressure and living cultures.
sensesIntro.cn: thrive 保留「牢牢抓住」这一个意象，让它蔓生为事业成功、植物健壮、压力下的强韧与兴盛的文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vine that has found the light and climbed over the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：找到阳光、一路爬过墙头的藤。

branches.en: The venture: businesses and people doing well.
branches.cn: 事业线：生意与人越来越好。

branches.en: The plant: roots that grip and shoots that climb.
branches.cn: 植物线：根系紧抓，枝条上扬。

branches.en: The strain: doing better exactly where others fail.
branches.cn: 压力线：恰在别人撑不住处表现出色。

branches.en: The culture: ideas and habits spreading and blooming.
branches.cn: 文化线：观念与习惯传播开来、开花结果。

branches.en: Commercial and botanical growth share one word.
branches.cn: 商业增长与植物生长共用一个词。

intro.en: Thrive stays simple; English adds -ing and the older irregular endings.

latinIntro.en: The word comes through Old Norse with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.

definition_zh: 铁路（美式）；铁路公司；强行推进
definition_en: a railway, especially in American English; the company or system that operates trains; to force something through quickly without proper discussion
core_image: 荒原上一列火车拖着长长的烟尘驶向地平线
scene: 西部小镇的站牌下，一条铁轨一直延伸到地平线。 The railroad brought goods and new families to the small town.
sceneCN: 这里 railroad 是「铁路（美式说法）」（第 1 个义项：供火车行驶的轨道与线路）；句意为铁路给这座小镇带来了货物和新的家庭。画面里可留意：站牌、伸向地平线的轨条、远去的车影。

pos.zh: 铁路（美式）；铁路公司；铁路系统
强行推进；迫使仓促通过

derivatives.zh: railroad 加 -er，指铁路员工或铁路经营者
railroad 加 -ing，指铁路运输业，也指强行推进的做法
railroad 加 -ed，指被仓促强行通过的

senses.title: A railway, in American use
senses.definition: a track of rails with its stations, signals and trains, the usual American word for a railway
senses.definitionCN: 带车站、信号与列车的轨道系统，美式英语对铁路的常用说法
senses.example: The railroad reached the coast in the eighteen eighties.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路在十九世纪八十年代修到了海边。
senses.why: American English joined rail and road to name the whole line, while British English preferred railway.
senses.whyCN: 美式英语把 rail 与 road 组合起来命名整条线路，而英式英语更爱用 railway。

senses.title: The company or system
senses.definition: the organization that owns and runs the trains and the line
senses.definitionCN: 拥有并经营列车与线路的机构
senses.example: He worked for the railroad for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在铁路公司工作了三十年。
senses.why: The physical line and the company that runs it share the name, as with many large networks.
senses.whyCN: 实体线路与经营它的公司在名字上不分，许多大型网络都是如此。

senses.title: To force something through
senses.titleCN: 强行推进；迫使仓促通过
senses.definition: to push a decision or a law through quickly, without proper debate
senses.definitionCN: 不经充分辩论就迅速推动一项决定或法律通过
senses.example: The bill was railroaded through the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这项议案被强行在委员会里仓促通过。
senses.why: The verb pictures a measure being pushed along like a train on a track, with no chance to stop it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把一项措施想象成轨道上的列车被一路推着走，没有停下的机会。

intro.en: Railroad is an English compound of rail and road, coined in the nineteenth century when lines of rail first crossed long distances.
intro.cn: railroad 是 rail 与 road 的英语复合词，十九世纪铁路线首次跨越长距离时被造出来。

items.en: Rail came from the Latin word for a straight rule, by way of French, and named the metal bar itself.
items.cn: rail 经法语来自拉丁语表示直尺的词，指的就是那根金属条。

items.en: Road is a native English word for a prepared way between places, from the same old root as ride.
items.cn: road 是英语本族词，指两地之间修好的通道，与 ride 同出一个古老词根。

items.en: The compound railroad named the road made of rails, a line laid across country for trains.
items.cn: 复合词 railroad 指由轨条铺成的路，一条横穿乡野供火车行驶的线路。

items.en: As lines crossed the continent in the nineteenth century, railroad became the standard American word.
items.cn: 十九世纪铁路线横贯大陆时，railroad 成了美国的标准说法。

items.en: The verb to railroad, meaning to push something through without debate, grew from the image of a train that cannot be stopped.
items.cn: 动词 railroad 意为不经辩论就强行推进，来自「停不下来的列车」这一意象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same compound; the near-meaning group gathers words for rail systems and forced decisions.
note.cn: 形近组收同一复合词的形式；近义组收表示铁路系统与强行决定的词。

entries.definition: The British word for the same system.
A single metal bar for train wheels.
entries.definitionCN: 供火车车轮行驶的一根金属条。

entries.definition: A person who works for a railroad.
The railroad business, or the act of forcing something through.
entries.definitionCN: 铁路运输业，或强行推进的做法。

entries.definition: A route of rails or wires between places.
entries.definitionCN: 两地之间的轨道或线路。

entries.definition: The pair of rails a train runs on.
entries.definitionCN: 火车行驶其上的那对钢轨。

entries.definition: A connected system of lines or routes.
entries.definitionCN: 相互连接的线路或路线系统。

entries.definition: To make someone decide or act too quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使某人过快决定或行动。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply rail plus road, a road made of rails; American English uses it where British English says railway.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 rail 加 road，即由轨条铺成的路；美式英语用它，而英式英语说 railway。

normal.en: Railroad is rail plus road, so the word literally says a road of rails.
normal.cn: railroad 是 rail 加 road，字面上就是「轨条铺成的路」。

normal.en: American speakers say railroad, British speakers say railway, and both describe the same line.
normal.cn: 美国人说 railroad，英国人说 railway，描述的是同一条线路。

normal.en: A railroad car is a single carriage, not a motor car on rails.
normal.cn: railroad car 指一节车厢，而不是在轨道上跑的汽车。

normal.en: To railroad a bill is to push it through so fast that nobody can examine it.
normal.cn: to railroad 一项议案，就是把它推得太快，没人来得及审查。

normal.en: Railroaded is the adjective for a decision made in that way, and it usually carries disapproval.
normal.cn: railroaded 是形容这样作出的决定的形容词，通常带有不赞成的意味。

abstract.en: Building a railroad across a continent is an act of faith in straight lines and fixed schedules.
abstract.cn: 横贯大陆修一条铁路，是对直线与固定时刻表的一次信念之举。

abstract.en: The same word means a line that connects people and a procedure that ignores them.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指连接人们的线路，也指无视人们的程序。

abstract.en: A railroaded decision is still a decision, which is why procedure matters as much as outcome.
abstract.cn: 被强行通过的决定仍然是决定，所以程序与结果同样重要。

examples.en: The railroad cut the journey from weeks to days.
examples.cn: 铁路把这段旅程从数周缩短到几天。

examples.en: She grew up in a house beside the railroad tracks.
examples.cn: 她在铁路轨道旁的一所房子里长大。

examples.en: The mayor tried to railroad the plan through the council.
examples.cn: 市长试图让议会在未充分讨论的情况下强行通过该计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐欧罗德」——一根根锐利的轨条连成一条长路，记住 railroad 是铁路。

root: rail（轨条，源自拉丁语 regula）+ road（路，英语本族词）复合而成，十九世纪出现；同族有 railway、railroader、railroading。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a road of rails; the senses divide into the American railway, the company that runs it, and a verb of forcing something through.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「由轨条铺成的路」；义项分为美式铁路、经营它的公司，以及强行推进的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a train trailing smoke toward the horizon across open country.
core.cn: 核心意象：一列拖着烟尘的火车穿过旷野驶向地平线。

branches.en: a line of steel running to the horizon
branches.cn: 延伸到地平线的一条钢线

branches.en: a station sign beside a single track
branches.cn: 单线轨道旁的一块站牌

branches.en: a timetable pinned in an office
branches.cn: 办公室里钉着的时刻表

branches.en: a gavel brought down before debate ends
branches.cn: 辩论结束前落下的法槌

branches.en: the physical line and the institution that owns it
branches.cn: 实体线路与拥有它的机构

intro.en: The compound joins a Latin-derived rail to a native road, and English endings extend it to people, business and forced decisions.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把源自拉丁语的 rail 与本族的 road 结合，英语词尾又把它扩展到人、行业与强行决定。

latinIntro.en: Only the first element has a Latin source, the word for a straight rule.
latinIntro.cn: 只有第一个成分有拉丁语来源，即表示直尺的词。

definition_zh: 手推车；购物车；马车；用车运送
definition_en: a small vehicle with wheels that is pushed by hand or pulled by an animal, used for carrying goods
core_image: 轮子上架一块平板：靠人力或牲口拖着走
scene: 超市的过道里，她一边看货架一边往前走。 She pushed the cart past the shelves and dropped a loaf of bread into it.
sceneCN: 这里 cart 指「购物车」（第 1 个义项：超市里用手推的载物车）；句意是她推着购物车经过货架，把一条面包放了进去。

derivatives.zh: 赶车人；车夫
用车运输；运费
一车之量

senses.title: A small vehicle pushed by hand
senses.definition: a small wheeled vehicle that a person pushes, used for carrying goods in shops or on streets
senses.definitionCN: 一种带轮的小型载物车，由人推着走，用于在商店或街道上运送东西
senses.example: She pushed the cart to the checkout counter.
senses.exampleCN: 她把购物车推到收银台。
senses.why: The core image is a flat board on wheels, and a hand-pushed trolley is that image in its simplest modern form.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是架在轮子上的平板，而人手推的购物车正是这一意象最简单的现代形态。

senses.title: A wagon pulled by an animal
senses.definition: a two-wheeled or four-wheeled vehicle pulled by a horse or other animal, used in farming and transport
senses.definitionCN: 由马或其他牲口拉动的两轮或四轮大车，用于农活和运输
senses.example: The farmer loaded the hay onto a wooden cart.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把干草装上一辆木制大车。
senses.why: Once the wheeled board is large enough to need a beast of burden, the same word covers the farm wagon.
senses.whyCN: 当带轮的平板大到需要牲口来拉动时，同一个词自然就覆盖了农用大车。

senses.title: To carry something with effort
senses.definition: to carry or move something in a cart, or to carry something heavy with obvious effort
senses.definitionCN: 用车子运送某物，或很费力地搬运重物
senses.example: They carted the old furniture up three flights of stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把那件旧家具费力地搬上三层楼。
senses.why: If a cart is the tool for moving loads, the verb names the whole act of hauling those loads.
senses.whyCN: 既然大车就是搬重物的工具，动词便顺势指代了整个搬运动作。

intro.en: Cart is a Germanic word that reached English from Old Norse rather than from Latin, which is why it has no Latin relatives in this entry.
intro.cn: cart 是日耳曼语词，经由古诺斯语进入英语，而不是来自拉丁语，所以本条没有拉丁同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed noun for a wheeled carrier, generally connected with the base that also produced car.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个表示带轮载具的原始日耳曼语名词，与产生 car 的词根相关。

items.en: Old Norse kartr named a small two-wheeled wagon and came south with Norse settlement in England.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kartr 指一种两轮小车，随北欧移民进入英格兰。

items.en: Cart is recorded in the thirteenth century as the everyday word for a farm or market wagon.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，cart 在十三世纪已有记录，是农用和集市运货车的日常说法。

items.en: The word spreads to any low wheeled platform, including hand carts used in towns.
items.cn: 此后该词扩展到任何低矮的带轮平台，包括城镇里使用的手推车。

items.en: Modern English adds the shopping cart, the golf cart and the verb sense of hauling something with effort.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上购物车、高尔夫球车，以及费力搬运的动词义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Germanic stem, while the meaning group gathers other wheeled carriers.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一日耳曼词干构成的词，近义组收的是其他带轮载具。

entries.definition: a person who drives or works with a cart
entries.definitionCN: 赶车人；以赶车为业的人

entries.definition: the work or charge of moving goods by cart
entries.definitionCN: 用车运输的工作或运费

entries.definition: as much as a cart can carry
a large four-wheeled vehicle for carrying heavy loads
entries.definitionCN: 运载重物的大型四轮车

entries.definition: a small wheeled frame or basket pushed by hand
entries.definitionCN: 用手推的带轮小车或篮子

entries.definition: a small hand cart with one wheel at the front
entries.definitionCN: 前部只有一个轮子的手推小车

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the link with car, the common compounds and the verb pattern of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用它与 car 的联系、常见复合词以及动词用法。

normal.en: Cart differs from car by one letter, and a cart is in effect a car stripped of its engine.
normal.cn: cart 比 car 只多一个字母，而大车实际上就是卸掉发动机的汽车。

normal.en: The fixed phrase shopping cart ties the word to the supermarket aisle.
normal.cn: 固定搭配 shopping cart 把这个词牢牢拴在超市过道上。

normal.en: The suffix -er in carter marks the person, exactly as in driver and worker.
normal.cn: carter 里的后缀 -er 表示人，与 driver、worker 的构词方式一样。

normal.en: Cart away and cart off both suggest taking something away in a loaded cart.
normal.cn: cart away 与 cart off 都表示用装满货的车把东西拉走。

normal.en: The plural carts and the third-person carts look identical, so only the sentence tells you which is which.
normal.cn: 复数 carts 与三单 carts 拼写相同，只能靠句子判断是名词还是动词。

abstract.en: Picture a squeaking wheel rolling down a supermarket aisle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只吱吱作响的轮子在超市过道里滚动。

abstract.en: Picture a horse straining against the shafts of a wooden cart.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹马绷紧车辕，拉着一辆木车。

abstract.en: Picture yourself heaving a load of bricks onto a low platform with wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象自己把一摞砖费力地抬上带轮的低矮平板。

examples.en: He loaded the boxes onto the cart.
examples.cn: 他把箱子装上了手推车。

examples.en: The farmer carted the hay to the barn.
examples.cn: 农夫把干草运到了谷仓。

examples.en: A cart blocked the narrow street.
examples.cn: 一辆大车堵住了狭窄的街道。

dict_mnemonic.text: cart 比 car 多一个 t：像一辆卸掉发动机的小汽车，只剩下带轮子的载货平板。

root: 古诺斯语 kartr（双轮车）借入中古英语，与 car 同出一支日耳曼语词，本义是带轮的载物工具。

sensesIntro.en: One core shape, a board on wheels, gives a hand trolley, an animal wagon and finally the act of hauling loads.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个核心形状，即架在轮子上的平板，先后长出手推车、牲口大车，最后长出搬运这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat board on wheels, moved by hand or by an animal.
core.cn: 核心意象：架在轮子上的平板，靠人力或牲口拖动。

branches.en: The hand-pushed trolley keeps the small size and the human power.
branches.cn: 手推车保留了小巧的尺寸和人力推动的方式。

branches.en: The wagon scales the same platform up until an animal supplies the pull.
branches.cn: 大车把同一块平板放大，直到改由牲口提供拉力。

branches.en: The verb turns the tool into the action of moving a load.
branches.cn: 动词义把工具转成了搬运货物的动作。

branches.en: Both nouns share wheels, a flat load bed and short-distance work.
branches.cn: 两个名词义都共享轮子、平载货面和短途作业这三个特征。

branches.en: Heavy hauling links the farm wagon with the effortful verb sense.
branches.cn: 沉重的拖运把农用大车与费力的动词义连在一起。

intro.en: Cart builds almost nothing with classical affixes; its family grows through inflection and compounding.
intro.cn: cart 几乎不用古典词缀构词，它的词族靠屈折变化和复合构词扩展。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin and has no Latin ancestor, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 该词源自日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: The cart is by the door.

items.meaning: more than one cart, or he carts

Carting stones all day is hard work.

items.meaning: a person who drives a cart

Cartage was added to the bill.
They bought a cartload of apples.

items.meaning: the wheel of a cart, or a sideways roll
items.example: The child turned a cartwheel on the grass.
items.exampleCN: 孩子在草地上翻了个侧手翻。

definition_zh: 刹车；制动器；踩刹车
definition_en: a device that slows or stops a vehicle
core_image: 车轮内侧被夹紧的金属片
scene: 下坡前他轻轻踩住刹车。 He held the brake gently before the slope.
sceneCN: 这里 brake 是「刹车」（第 1 个义项：使车辆减速或停下的装置）；句意是下坡前他轻轻踩住刹车。

derivatives.zh: 制动
制动员

senses.title: A device that stops a vehicle
senses.definition: a part that slows or stops a wheel
senses.definitionCN: 使车轮减速或停下的部件
senses.example: He held the brake gently before the slope.
senses.exampleCN: 下坡前他轻轻踩住刹车。
senses.why: This is the earliest sense, naming the machine part.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早的义项，指机器的部件。

senses.title: To slow with the brakes

senses.definitionCN: 用刹车使车辆减速或停下
senses.example: She braked hard at the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 她在路口猛踩了一脚刹车。
senses.why: The device turned into a verb for using it.
senses.whyCN: 这个装置后来转化成使用它的动词。

senses.title: Something that slows progress
senses.definition: something that keeps an activity from moving fast
senses.definitionCN: 使某项活动无法快速推进的东西
senses.example: High costs are a brake on growth.
senses.exampleCN: 高昂的成本是增长的阻碍。
senses.why: A brake on a wheel became a picture for any check.
senses.whyCN: 车轮上的制动被用来比喻任何制约。

intro.cn: brake 最初指打麻的工具，后来指制约车轮的部件。

items.en: brake covers the part and the act of slowing.
items.cn: 如今 brake 兼指部件与减速动作。
