examples.en: High costs are a brake on growth.
examples.cn: 高昂的成本是增长的阻碍。

dict_mnemonic.text: brake 与 break 同音，但 brake 里有 a，像一脚踩下去「啊」地停住，记住它是刹车。

root: brake 源自古荷兰语 braeke，最初指打麻的工具，中古英语进入英语后指作用于车轮的制动杆，工业时代成为车辆制动的通称，并引申出「阻碍」的抽象义。

sensesIntro.en: A machine part, the act of slowing and any check on progress.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个机械部件、减速的动作、对进展的任何制约。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metal pad pressed against a turning wheel.
core.cn: 核心意象：金属片夹住转动的车轮。

branches.en: the front brake
branches.cn: 前刹车

branches.en: brake lights
branches.cn: 刹车灯

branches.en: brake at the corner
branches.cn: 在转弯处刹车

branches.en: a brake on growth
branches.cn: 增长的阻碍

branches.en: an emergency brake
branches.cn: 紧急制动

intro.en: Brake forms nouns with -ing and -man.
intro.cn: brake 加 -ing 与 -man 构成名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Dutch; the Latin items below are related only in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自荷兰语，下面的拉丁词只在意思上相关。

definition_zh: 火山；火山口；潜伏的危机
definition_en: a mountain with a vent in the earth, from which lava, ash and hot gas can burst out
core_image: 山顶裂开一道口子，滚烫的岩浆顺着山坡淌下来
scene: 岛上的居民半夜被闷响惊醒，窗外山顶正冒出暗红色的光。 Through the night, the volcano poured glowing lava down its northern slope.
sceneCN: 这里 volcano 是「火山」（第 1 个义项：能够喷出熔岩与火山灰的山体）；句意为整夜里火山把发光的熔岩顺着北坡倾泻下来。山顶裂开冒红光的那幅画就是这个词给人的印象。

pos.zh: 火山；火山口；潜伏的危机

collocations.zh: 怒气的火山：一触即发的情绪

derivatives.zh: 由 volcano 加 -ic 构成，义为「火山的；火山般的」
加 -ally 构成，义为「火山似地；剧烈地」
加 -ism 构成，义为「火山作用；火山现象」
加 -logy 构成，义为「火山学」
加 -logist 构成，义为「火山学家」

senses.title: A mountain that can erupt
senses.definition: a mountain or hill with an opening in the earth through which lava, ash and gas escape
senses.definitionCN: 地表有出口、能喷出熔岩、火山灰与气体的山体
senses.example: Through the night, the volcano poured glowing lava down its northern slope.
senses.exampleCN: 整夜里，火山把发光的熔岩顺着北坡倾泻下来。
senses.why: The Italian island of Vulcano was thought to be the workshop of the fire god, and the whole kind of mountain took its name.
senses.whyCN: 意大利小岛武尔卡诺被认为火神的工作场，这一类山便借用了它的名字。

senses.title: The vent of a volcano
senses.definition: the vent or opening itself, rather than the whole cone around it
senses.definitionCN: 火山喷出口本身，而非周边整座锥体
senses.example: Sensors were lowered into the volcano to measure the rising heat.
senses.exampleCN: 为测量上升的热量，探测器被放进火山口里。
senses.why: The name points first at the hole through which fire comes up; the mountain around it was named afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最先指的是火冒出来的那个口子，周围的山体后来才被一并命名。

senses.title: The god of fire in old belief
senses.definition: in older use, the workshop of the fire god or the fire believed to burn beneath the ground
senses.definitionCN: 早期用法里指火神的作坊，或被认为在地下燃烧的火
senses.example: Old sailors told of a volcano beneath the sea where the fire god worked.
senses.exampleCN: 老水手讲起海面之下有座火山，火神就在那里干活。
senses.why: Before geology, fire from the ground was explained by a god; Vulcan ruled that fire and his name stayed in the mountain.
senses.whyCN: 在地质学出现以前，地下冒出的火用神来解释；火神伏尔甘掌管这火，他的名字留在了山上。

senses.title: The volcanic adjective
senses.definition: relating to, or produced by, a volcano, as in volcanic rock and volcanic ash
senses.definitionCN: 与火山有关的、由火山产生的，如火山岩与火山灰
senses.example: The village sits on volcanic rock that keeps the soil rich.
senses.exampleCN: 村庄坐落在使土壤肥沃的火山岩上。
senses.why: Adding -ic turns the mountain into a describing word, so the adjective covers everything a volcano makes.
senses.whyCN: 加上 -ic，山就变成修饰词，于是这个词覆盖了火山产出的一切。

senses.title: A temper ready to blow
senses.titleCN: 火山般的情绪；一触即发
senses.definition: a state of feeling or a situation that is under pressure and may explode at any moment
senses.definitionCN: 受压、随时可能爆发的情绪或局面
senses.example: His anger was a volcano that no one dared to set off.
senses.exampleCN: 他的怒气像一座火山，没人敢去点燃。
senses.why: A volcano rests quietly for years and then bursts without warning; that is exactly how a held-in temper behaves.
senses.whyCN: 火山安静多年却毫无预警地爆发，忍耐着的脾气正是这副样子。

intro.en: Volcano is named after the small island of Vulcano, which was taken as the chimney of the fire god.
intro.cn: volcano 以小岛武尔卡诺命名，古代认为那里是火神的烟囱。

items.en: Vulcanus was the Roman god of fire and of metalwork, and his name is the seed of the word.
items.cn: Vulcanus 是罗马的火与锻造之神，这个名字就是本词的种子。

items.en: Vulcano, one of the Aeolian Islands, was seen as a workshop where smoke rose from the ground.
items.cn: 武尔卡诺是伊奥利亚群岛之一，人们把那里看作地面冒烟的作坊。

items.en: Deeper roots of Vulcanus are debated; some link it to a word for lightning, but no solution is settled.
items.cn: Vulcanus 更早的来源有争议，有人认为与表示闪电的词有关，但尚无定论。

items.en: In the sixteenth century Italian writers used vulcano for any fire-breathing mountain, and the range of meaning widened.
items.cn: 十六世纪意大利作家用 vulcano 指任何喷火的山，这个词的所指扩大。

items.en: English adopted the word in the seventeenth century and kept the plural volcanoes in common use.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入该词，复数 volcanoes 成为通用形式。

items.en: Geology then split the image into the cone, its vent, its products and the metaphor of exploding feeling.
items.cn: 此后地质学把这个形象分成山锥、喷口、产物以及「情绪爆发」的比喻。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the name of the fire god, the second the other landforms and fire words near it.
note.cn: 第一组收以火神之名为基础的词，第二组收相近的地貌词与火相关词。

entries.definition: The usual plural form of the noun.
The adjective meaning of or made by a volcano.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「火山的、由火山造成的」。

entries.definition: The Roman fire god whose name the mountain carries.
entries.definitionCN: 罗马火神，这座山沿用了他的名字。

entries.definition: The noun for the whole set of volcanic processes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指火山活动的总体过程。

entries.definition: The bowl-shaped opening at the top of a volcano.
The hot melted rock that a volcano pours out.
The melted rock still below the ground, not yet erupted.
entries.definitionCN: 尚在地下、尚未喷出的岩浆。

entries.definition: Shaking of the ground, often in the same regions as volcanoes.
entries.definitionCN: 地震，常与火山出现在同一区域。

normalIntro.en: One named island, one fire god, and a set of ordinary English endings explain the whole family.
normalIntro.cn: 一座得名的小岛、一位火神，加上普通英语后缀，就能解释整个词族。

normal.en: Volcano, volcanic and volcanology all rest on the god Vulcan.
normal.cn: volcano、volcanic、volcanology 都建立在火神伏尔甘的名字上。

normal.en: The plural is volcanoes, with an e before the s.
normal.cn: 复数是 volcanoes，s 前要加 e。

normal.en: Lava is outside, magma is inside; both come from a volcano.
normal.cn: lava 在地上，magma 在地下，两者都出自火山。

normal.en: An active volcano erupts now, a dormant one sleeps.
normal.cn: active volcano 现在喷发，dormant volcano 正在沉睡。

normal.en: Used of people, the word keeps the image: a volcano of anger.
normal.cn: 用于人时意象仍在：volcano of anger（怒火如火山）。

abstract.en: See a dark cone at night with one red line running down its side.
abstract.cn: 想夜里一座黑色的锥形山，侧面拖着一条红线。

abstract.en: Hear a low rumble under the floor long before anything is seen.
abstract.cn: 想在地面之下先听到低沉的闷响，许久之后才见东西。

abstract.en: Feel a held-in temper waiting, quiet and hot, behind a shut door.
abstract.cn: 感受一扇关着的门后，压抑的脾气安静而灼热地等着。

examples.en: The volcano has been quiet for two hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座火山已经安静了两百年。

examples.en: Ash from the volcano covered the fields for weeks.
examples.cn: 火山灰覆盖田野达数周之久。

examples.en: Scientists mapped the inside of the volcano with sound waves.
examples.cn: 科学家用声波绘制了火山内部的结构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「火山口的老肯」——老肯守在火山口边，看见红汤往外冒。

root: 拉丁语 Vulcanus（罗马火神）→ 意大利语 vulcano（火山，源自小岛武尔卡诺）→ 英语 volcano；更早词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a named island and a god, then covers the mountain, its opening, what it produces, and the metaphor of feelings about to burst.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一座得名的小岛与一位神出发，先指山体，再指喷口、火山产物，最后比喻随时爆发的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mountain with a red crack at the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：山顶有一道红色裂口的山。

branches.en: The mountain branch: a cone pouring lava down its slope.
branches.cn: 山体分支：熔岩顺坡流下的锥形山。

branches.en: The opening branch: the vent itself, measured and studied.
branches.cn: 开口分支：喷口本身，被测量与研究。

branches.en: The old belief branch: the fire god at work underground.
branches.cn: 旧信仰分支：火神在地下干活。

branches.en: The adjective branch: volcanic rock under a village.
branches.cn: 形容词分支：村庄下方的火山岩。

branches.en: The temper branch: anger that no one dares to set off.
branches.cn: 脾气分支：没人敢点燃的怒火。

intro.en: Volcan- is a name, not a Latin meaning; the endings -o, -ic, -ism and -ology do the building after the name was borrowed.
intro.cn: volcan- 是一个专名而非拉丁义素；后缀 -o、-ic、-ism、-ology 在名字借入后承担构词。

latinIntro.en: The name goes back to the Roman god Vulcanus; a Latin god name is recorded, so only the deeper root is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 名字上溯到罗马神名 Vulcanus；神名有文献记录，只有更早词根不确定。

items.example: The god gave his name to the island.
items.exampleCN: 这位神把自己的名字给了那座岛。
武尔卡诺岛位于西西里附近。

items.example: The Italian ending stayed on the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语词尾保留在英语名词上。

items.example: An active volcano is watched day and night.

definition_zh: 献身；挚爱；虔诚；专注
definition_en: deep love and loyalty, or the act of giving yourself to something
core_image: 神龛前一小盏长明灯，油快尽了还亮着
scene: 小教堂里那盏灯整夜亮着，守夜的人换了一个又一个。 Her devotion to the old school never faded.
sceneCN: 这里 devotion 指「挚爱」（第 2 个义项：深厚的感情与忠诚）；句意是她对那所老学校的挚爱从未消退。

derivatives.zh: 致力于；献身
忠诚的；挚爱的
忠实地
爱好者；信徒
虔诚的；礼拜的

senses.title: Giving yourself to a cause
senses.definition: the act of giving your time and energy completely to something
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的时间与精力完全投入某事物的行为
senses.example: His devotion to the research left little time for sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这项研究的投入让他几乎没时间睡觉。
senses.why: A cause can hold a person the way a fire holds a room.
senses.whyCN: 一项事业能占据一个人，就像火占据一间屋。

senses.title: Deep love and loyalty
senses.definition: strong love and loyalty toward a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物深厚的爱与忠诚
senses.example: Her devotion to the old school never faded.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那所老学校的挚爱从未消退。
senses.why: Love that keeps returning is love that has become a habit of the heart.
senses.whyCN: 不断回来的爱，已经成了心里的习惯。

senses.title: Religious faithfulness
senses.definition: strong religious feeling shown in prayer and practice
senses.definitionCN: 在祈祷与修行中表现出的强烈宗教情感
senses.example: The old woman's devotion was visible in her daily prayers.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老妇人的虔诚在她每日的祈祷里看得见。
senses.why: A small flame kept alive says more than a loud sermon.
senses.whyCN: 一盏被守住的小火，比一场响亮的布道说得更多。

intro.en: Devotion comes from Latin devotio, a vow or dedication, from devovere, to vow away, and it entered English through French.
intro.cn: devotion 来自拉丁语 devotio（许愿、奉献），源自动词 devovere（许愿献出），经法语进入英语。

items.en: Devotio first named a solemn vow that set a person apart.
items.cn: devotio 最初指把人分别出来的郑重誓言。

items.en: It could also mean a curse, when a person was vowed to harm.
items.cn: 当一个人被许愿交给伤害时，它也能指诅咒。

items.en: French devotion narrowed to religious dedication.
items.cn: 法语 devotion 收窄为宗教上的虔敬。

items.en: English used it for worship and for loyalty to a person.
items.cn: 英语用它表示礼拜，也表示对人的忠诚。

items.en: It now covers love, duty, study and any steady attachment.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖爱、责任、学业以及任何稳定的依恋。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the devot stem, and the meaning group names loyalty, commitment and piety.
note.cn: 形近组共用 devot 这个词干，近义组则指忠诚、投入与虔敬。

entries.definition: to give time or energy to something
entries.definitionCN: 把时间或精力给某事物

entries.definition: showing deep love or loyalty
a very keen supporter
faithfulness to a person or group
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某群体的忠实

entries.definition: the act of giving time to a purpose
deep respect shown in religion
entries.definitionCN: 在宗教中表现出的深切敬意

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a small flame in a chapel and end with a teacher who never stops caring.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从小教堂里的一点火苗开始，落到一位从不停下关心的老师。

normal.en: Devotion is the noun of a promise that kept being paid.
normal.cn: devotion 是一个一直有人去还的承诺的名词。

normal.en: Love becomes devotion when it comes back the next morning.
normal.cn: 爱在第二天早上还回来，就成了挚爱。

normal.en: The oil is low, and the flame still stands.
normal.cn: 油快见底了，火苗还立着。

normal.en: A quiet room can hold more prayer than a full one.
normal.cn: 一间安静的屋子，能装下比满屋人更多的祈祷。

normal.en: Duty done daily looks dull and is the hardest kind.
normal.cn: 每天做的责任看着很闷，却也是最难的一种。

abstract.en: Picture a red glass cup holding one small flame.
abstract.cn: 想象一只红玻璃杯盛着一小簇火苗。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pouring the last of the oil.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手倒进最后一点油。

abstract.en: Picture a desk used so long that the varnish is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一张用得太久、漆都磨没了的书桌。

examples.en: His devotion to the research left little time for sleep.
examples.cn: 他对这项研究的投入让他几乎没时间睡觉。

examples.en: Her devotion to the old school never faded.
examples.cn: 她对那所老学校的挚爱从未消退。

examples.en: The old woman's devotion was visible in her daily prayers.
examples.cn: 那位老妇人的虔诚在她每日的祈祷里看得见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 devotion 记成「地沃神」：de 是交给，vot 是誓愿，-ion 是状态，把心交给一个誓愿，就是献身与挚爱。

root: 来自拉丁语 devotio，源自动词 devovere（许愿献出），由 de-（彻底）与 vovere（立誓）组成，经法语进入英语。本义是郑重许愿、分别出来献给神，后来用于宗教虔敬，也扩展到对人的挚爱与对事业的献身。

sensesIntro.en: From hours given to a cause, to love that keeps returning, to a small flame kept burning.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把时间交给一项事业，到不断回来的爱，再到一盏被守住的小火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small lamp kept alight in front of a shrine.
core.cn: 核心意象：神龛前一小盏一直亮着的灯。

branches.en: The first sense is the effort that keeps being given.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是不断被交出去的那份力气。

branches.en: The second sense is the warmth that makes the giving easy.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是让这份给予变得容易的温度。

branches.en: The third sense is the flame that the giving is aimed at.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是这份给予所朝向的那簇火。

branches.en: Effort without love burns out, and love without effort cools.
branches.cn: 没有爱的投入会烧尽，没有投入的爱会变凉。

branches.en: A person and a faith can both be loved with the same steadiness.
branches.cn: 对一个人与对一种信仰，能用同一种稳定去爱。

intro.en: Devotion belongs to a family about vows, steady love and faithful practice.
intro.cn: devotion 属于一族词，围绕誓言、稳定的爱与忠实的修行。

latinIntro.en: The base is vovere, to vow, and de- marks the offering as complete.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 vovere（立誓），前缀 de- 表示这份奉献是彻底的。

items.example: She is a devotee of jazz.

items.exampleCN: 他的虔敬让修士们印象深刻。

definition_zh: 嫉妒；嫉妒心；吃醋；羡慕
definition_en: the feeling of being unhappy because someone has something you want, or may take someone you love
core_image: 一个人站在门外，从门缝往里看，屋里的人在笑
scene: 她看到朋友的照片里多了一张陌生的脸，心一下沉下去。 A wave of jealousy swept over her when she saw the photo.
sceneCN: 这里 jealousy 是「嫉妒」（第 1 个义项：因别人拥有自己想要之物而不快），句意为看到那张照片时一阵嫉妒涌上来。画面里的物件：手机里的照片、陌生的脸。

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词基础形式，义为「嫉妒的」
由 jealous 加 -ly 构成，义为「嫉妒地」
由 jealous 加 -ness 构成，义为「嫉妒的状态」

senses.title: Resentment at another's goods
senses.definition: the unhappy feeling that comes from seeing someone else have what you want
senses.definitionCN: 看到别人拥有你想要的而产生的难受心情
senses.example: Jealousy made him refuse to congratulate her.
senses.exampleCN: 嫉妒使他不肯向她道贺。
senses.why: The noun names the emotion itself, while the adjective names the person who feels it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指情感本身，而形容词指感到这种情感的人。

senses.title: Fear of a rival
senses.definition: the anxious feeling that someone you love prefers another person
senses.definitionCN: 担心所爱的人更喜欢别人的焦虑心情
senses.example: His jealousy grew every time she mentioned the new colleague.
senses.exampleCN: 她每提一次那位新同事，他的醋意就多一分。
senses.why: This is the narrowest and oldest emotional sense, coming from the word for a rival.
senses.whyCN: 这是最窄也最古老的情感义，来自表示情敌的那个词。

senses.title: Envy of a position
senses.definition: a milder feeling of wanting the situation another person enjoys
senses.definitionCN: 较轻的、想要别人所处境况的心情
senses.example: There is some jealousy behind his kind words.
senses.exampleCN: 他好话背后有一点羡慕。
senses.why: English lets the same noun cover a whole range from admiration to resentment.
senses.whyCN: 英语让这个名词覆盖从钦佩到怨恨的整段区间。

senses.title: A watchful protectiveness
senses.definition: careful guarding of something one values, without anger
senses.definitionCN: 对珍视之物的谨慎守护，不带怒意
senses.example: The rules were kept with a certain jealousy.
senses.exampleCN: 这些规矩被相当小心的珍视着。
senses.why: Guarding closely is the noun's older, cooler sense of keeping watch.
senses.whyCN: 紧守不放是这个名词较古老也较冷静的「看护」义。

senses.title: An instance of the feeling
senses.definition: a particular occasion or cause of such a feeling, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指具体的嫉妒事件或让人嫉妒的原因
senses.example: The old jealousies between the two villages never died.
senses.exampleCN: 两个村子之间旧日的嫉妒从未消失。
senses.why: Plural use turns the mood into countable events with a history.
senses.whyCN: 复数把这种情绪变成有来历、可数的事件。

intro.en: Jealousy follows the adjective jealous, from Old French gelos and Latin zelus, itself from Greek zelos.
intro.cn: jealousy 顺着形容词 jealous 而来，源头是古法语 gelos、拉丁语 zelus，更远是希腊语 zelos。

items.en: zelos named eager rivalry and zeal.
items.cn: zelos 指热烈的争胜与热忱。

items.en: zelus was the Latin form used in church and poetic writing.
items.cn: zelus 是其拉丁形式，见于宗教与诗文。

items.en: gelos named a jealous person and gelosie the feeling.
items.cn: gelos 指嫉妒的人，gelosie 指这种心情。

items.en: English borrowed jealousy as the noun of the emotion.
items.cn: 英语借入 jealousy 作为这种情感的名词。

items.en: The plural jealousies names repeated outbreaks of the feeling.
items.cn: 复数 jealousies 指这种情感反复出现。

note.en: The look-alike group is jealous plus its endings; the near-meaning group holds envy and distrust.
note.cn: 形近组是 jealous 及其词尾形式；近义组收羡慕与不信任相关词。

entries.definition: Feeling unhappy about another's good fortune.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「嫉妒的」，本词的基础形式。

entries.definition: In a jealous or watchful manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「嫉妒地；小心地」，同族。

entries.definition: The quality of being jealous.
entries.definitionCN: 由 jealous 加 -ness 构成，义为「嫉妒的状态」。

entries.definition: The wish to have what another has.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「羡慕；嫉妒」，更侧重想要。

entries.definition: Bitter anger at unfair treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「怨恨」，起因是不公而非比较。

entries.definition: A lack of trust in someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「不信任」，没有对比成分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks place the noun after the adjective and keep the picture of watching a door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把名词放在形容词之后，并保留「从门缝里看」的画面。

normal.en: Jealousy is the noun built on jealous.
normal.cn: jealousy 是在 jealous 上构成的名词。

normal.en: Greek zelos gave zeal and jealousy alike.
normal.cn: 希腊语 zelos 同时生出 zeal 与 jealousy。

normal.en: A fit of jealousy is a sudden burst of it.
normal.cn: a fit of jealousy 就是一阵嫉妒。

normal.en: Out of jealousy, he said nothing.
normal.cn: 出于嫉妒，他什么也没说。

normal.en: Repeated outbursts become jealousies in the plural.
normal.cn: 反复发作就能用复数 jealousies。

abstract.en: Jealousy is a scale that weighs only other people.
abstract.cn: 嫉妒是一台只称别人的秤。

abstract.en: The room is warm and the watcher is outside.
abstract.cn: 屋里是暖的，看的人在外面。

abstract.en: Envy wants the thing; jealousy fears the loss.
abstract.cn: 羡慕想要那个东西，嫉妒怕失去。

examples.en: He could not hide his jealousy at the news.
examples.cn: 听到这消息他藏不住嫉妒。

examples.en: Professional jealousy is common among writers.
examples.cn: 作家之间同行相嫉很常见。

examples.en: Their old jealousies were finally forgotten.
examples.cn: 他们旧日的那些嫉妒终于被忘了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「急了谁」—— 嫉妒一起，心里急得不知该怪谁

root: 希腊语 zelos「争胜；热忱」→ 拉丁语 zelus → 古法语 gelosie → 中古英语 jealousy。同族有 jealous、jealously、jealousness，同源近亲 zeal。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: resentment at another's goods, fear of a rival, mild envy, a watchful protectiveness, and countable outbreaks of the feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：对别人所得的怨恨、怕情敌的吃醋、轻微羡慕、小心的珍视，以及可数的嫉妒事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watcher outside a lit window watching people laugh.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗外的人看着屋里的人在笑。

branches.en: THE NEWS: no word of congratulation offered.
branches.cn: 好消息这条线：一句道贺也没说。

branches.en: THE COLLEAGUE: one name repeated too often.
branches.cn: 同事这条线：一个名字被提得太多次。

branches.en: THE COMPLIMENT: praise with a hard edge.
branches.cn: 称赞这条线：好话里带刺。

branches.en: THE RULES: kept with unusual care.
branches.cn: 规矩这条线：被格外小心地守。

branches.en: THE VILLAGES: quarrels that never ended.
branches.cn: 村子这条线：从未结束的旧怨。

intro.en: Jealousy is the adjective jealous with a noun ending; the root itself is Greek via Latin and French.
intro.cn: jealousy 是形容词 jealous 加名词词尾，词根本身经法语、拉丁语来自希腊语。

latinIntro.en: Latin zelus supplies the stem behind the English -ous form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 zelus 提供了英语 -ous 形式背后的词干。

items.example: The Roman form of the word.

definition_zh: 小号；喇叭；号声；大声宣布
definition_en: a brass instrument with a bright high sound, or to announce something loudly
core_image: 一支铜号举向天空，喇叭口亮得能照出人脸
scene: 山头的风把旗子吹得笔直，一个少年举起手里的铜管准备吹响。 A trumpet sounded from the hill before the race began.
sceneCN: 这里 trumpet 是「小号；喇叭」（第 1 个义项：声音明亮高亢的铜管乐器）；句意为比赛开始前山上响起了号声。少年举向天空的那支铜号，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 trumpet 加 -er 构成，义为「小号手」
由 trumpet 加 -ing 构成，义为「号声；大肆宣扬」
与 trumpet 音近的动词，义为「打出（王牌）」

senses.title: The bright brass horn
senses.definition: a brass instrument made of a long tube with a wide bell, played by blowing
senses.definitionCN: 由长管与宽喇叭口组成、靠吹奏发声的铜管乐器
senses.example: A trumpet sounded from the hill before the race began.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛开始前，山上响起了号声。
senses.why: The old French word trump named a horn made of a tube, and English made trumpet from its smaller form.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 trump 指用管子做成的号，英语用小称形式造出 trumpet。

senses.title: The voice of an elephant
senses.definition: the loud call of an elephant, like a horn blast
senses.definitionCN: 大象响亮的叫声，像一阵号声
senses.example: We heard an elephant trumpet across the water.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见一头大象隔着水吼叫。
senses.why: A trumpet is loud and carries far, so the great call of an elephant borrowed its name.
senses.whyCN: 小号响亮且能传很远，于是大象的大叫也借用了它的名字。

senses.title: Announcing loudly
senses.definition: to make something known as widely and loudly as possible
senses.definitionCN: 尽可能广泛响亮地让某事为人所知
senses.example: The papers trumpeted the discovery of the sunken ship.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸大肆宣扬这艘沉船的发现。
senses.why: The instrument once called people to hear an announcement, so the verb now means shouting news.
senses.whyCN: 这种乐器曾把人们叫来听通告，于是动词如今意为大声传消息。

intro.en: Trumpet is a diminutive of the old French trump, the name of a long horn used to call and to announce.
intro.cn: trumpet 是古法语 trump 的小称形式，后者是用于召唤与宣告的长号的名字。

items.en: Trompe named a horn or a pipe, and the verb tromper meant to play such a horn.
items.cn: trompe 指号或管，动词 tromper 意为吹这种号。

items.en: The diminutive trumpet named a smaller, clearer horn used by soldiers and heralds.
items.cn: 小称 trumpet 指士兵与传令官使用的小而清亮的号。

items.en: English took the word as trumpet, both the instrument and its call.
items.cn: 英语以 trumpet 借入这个词，既指乐器也指号声。

items.en: The verb to trumpet, meaning to proclaim, grew out of the herald's use.
items.cn: 动词 trumpet 意为宣扬，出自传令官的用法。

items.en: Naturalists compared the elephant's call to a horn, giving a second noun sense.
items.cn: 博物学家把象叫比作号声，于是多了第二个名词义项。

note.en: The first group shares the trumpet stem, the second holds other brass and wind words.
note.cn: 第一组共享 trumpet 词干，第二组收其他铜管与吹奏乐器词。

entries.definition: A person who plays the trumpet.
The sound of a trumpet or a loud call.
To play a winning card.
A simple tube blown to make a call.
A small horn used for signals in an army.
A long brass instrument with a slide.

normalIntro.en: Trumpet is a small trumpet: the word starts like a blare and ends with a snapped -et.
normalIntro.cn: trumpet 就是小号的号：词头像吹响的一声，结尾是一个短促的 -et。

normal.en: The -et ending marks a smaller thing, as in pocket and booklet.
normal.cn: -et 结尾标记较小之物，如 pocket 与 booklet。

normal.en: A trumpeter is the player, the trumpet is the horn.
normal.cn: trumpeter 是吹的人，trumpet 是那把号。

normal.en: To trumpet news is to blow it out loud.
normal.cn: trumpet news 就是把消息大声吹出去。

normal.en: The past form simply adds ed: trumpeted.
normal.cn: 过去式直接加 ed：trumpeted。

normal.en: The elephant's trumpet needs no instrument at all.
normal.cn: 大象的 trumpet 根本不需要乐器。

abstract.en: A bright bell of brass pointed at the sky.
abstract.cn: 一支朝向天空的亮铜喇叭口。

abstract.en: A single high note crossing a valley.
abstract.cn: 一个高音越过山谷。

abstract.en: A voice that carries further than the room allows.
abstract.cn: 一个传出房间之外的声音。

examples.en: A trumpet and two drums opened the ceremony.
examples.cn: 一支小号和两面鼓拉开了典礼的序幕。

examples.en: Far off, an elephant trumpeted in the dark.
examples.cn: 远处，一头大象在黑暗中吼叫。

examples.en: The company trumpeted its success on every poster in town.
examples.cn: 这家公司在城里每张海报上宣扬自己的成功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹喇叭」的那声「特郎」——trumpet 就是小号，一吹就响遍全山。

root: 古法语 trompe（号、管）的小称 trumpet，动词 tromper 意为吹号；同族词有 trumpeter、trumpeting、trump。

sensesIntro.en: First the instrument, then the elephant call that copies it, then the act of announcing loudly.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是乐器，再是模仿它的象吼，最后是大声宣告的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brass bell pointed at the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：朝向天空的铜喇叭口。

branches.en: The instrument branch: tube, breath, and bell.
branches.cn: 乐器分支：管、气息与喇叭口。

branches.en: The animal branch: a horn a body can grow.
branches.cn: 动物分支：身体自带的号。

branches.en: The announcing branch: a call becomes a claim.
branches.cn: 宣告分支：号声变成声明。

branches.en: The herald branch: the horn once gathered a crowd.
branches.cn: 传令分支：号角曾招来人群。

branches.en: The sound branch: both are loud and far-reaching.
branches.cn: 声音分支：两者都响亮而传得远。

intro.en: Trumpet is an Old French stem with a diminutive ending, and English adds -er and -ing around it.
intro.cn: trumpet 是带小称词尾的古法语词干，英语在它周围加了 -er 与 -ing。

latinIntro.en: The word is French rather than Latin, but the horn words below belong to the same sound world.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词出自法语而非拉丁语，但下面的号角词汇属于同一个声音世界。

items.example: The stem names the long tube itself.
It marks the smaller, brighter horn.
The noun and the verb share one form.

items.exampleCN: 两座塔上的号声互相应答。

items.example: They trumpeted the result at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 他们在黎明时宣布了结果。

definition_zh: 不稳的；摇晃的；颤抖的；不坚定的；不稳重的
definition_en: likely to move or fall, or changing and not dependable
core_image: 桌腿短了一截，桌面一直在轻轻晃
scene: 手术后第三天，老人扶着床沿想站起来，脚下却总是发飘。 His walk is still unsteady after the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 unsteady 是「摇晃的」（第 1 个义项：站不稳、走不稳）；句意为手术后他走起路来仍然东摇西晃。桌面一直轻轻晃的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「摇晃地；颤巍巍地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不稳；摇晃」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「稳的；平稳的」
肯定形式加 -ly，义为「平稳地；持续地」

senses.title: A support that moves under weight
senses.definition: not firm on its base, so that it moves when used
senses.definitionCN: 底座不牢，一用就晃动
senses.example: The ladder was unsteady on the wet floor.
senses.exampleCN: 梯子在湿滑的地上放不稳。
senses.why: The prefix means not, and steady comes from stead, a fixed place; unsteady is therefore without a firm place to stand.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，steady 源自 stead（固定的位置）；因此 unsteady 就是「没有一个稳稳的立足点」。

senses.title: A body that cannot keep its balance
senses.definition: used of walking or standing that cannot keep balance
senses.definitionCN: 形容走路或站立时保持不住平衡
senses.example: He was still unsteady after the long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 久病之后他走路仍然摇晃。
senses.why: A body out of its stead is the oldest and most physical sense: no fixed place for the feet.
senses.whyCN: 身体离开了固定的位置，是这个词最古老也最具体的一层：脚下没有稳当地儿。

senses.title: A hand or voice that shakes
senses.definition: used of hands or voices that tremble from weakness or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 形容因虚弱或情绪而颤动的双手或声音
senses.example: Her unsteady hand spilled the water.
senses.exampleCN: 她发抖的手把水洒了出来。
senses.why: A hand without a firm place to rest shakes, just as the ladder without a firm base rocks.
senses.whyCN: 手找不到稳稳搁置的地方就会抖，这与梯子没有稳当底座就会摇是同一个道理。

senses.title: Behaviour that changes without warning
senses.definition: used of prices, growth, or behaviour that keeps changing
senses.definitionCN: 形容价格、增长或行为反复变化
senses.example: The unsteady demand made planning difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 起伏不定的需求让做计划变得困难。
senses.why: What rocks instead of holding a line gives the number-driven sense of a trend that will not stay level.
senses.whyCN: 摇来摇去而不沿一条直线的东西，就给出了「数值留不住水平」这层走势义。

senses.title: A decision or loyalty that wavers
senses.definition: used of faith or support that may give way at any moment
senses.definitionCN: 形容随时可能动摇的信念或支持
senses.example: Their unsteady support worried the campaign team.
senses.exampleCN: 他们摇摆不定的支持让竞选团队很担心。
senses.why: Support that is not fixed in place is the last extension: the same lack of a firm footing, now in feeling.
senses.whyCN: 没有固定下来的支持是最后一层延伸：还是那种缺了稳固落点的状态，只不过发生在心里。

intro.en: A native prefix over a very old adjective formed from the English noun stead.
intro.cn: 本土前缀压在由一个极古老的英语名词 stead 构成的形容词上。

items.en: Stede meant a place or position, and the adjective stedig meant placed, fixed.
items.cn: stede 意为「地方、位置」，形容词 stedig 意为「安置好的、固定的」。

items.en: The adjective now spelled steady already described what holds its place.
items.cn: 后来拼作 steady 的这个形容词，当时已经用来形容「守得住原位」的东西。

items.en: The spelling steady settles, and stead survives mostly in the phrase in someone's stead.
items.cn: steady 的拼写在这一时期定型，stead 则主要保留在 in someone's stead 这一短语里。

items.en: Unsteady is formed with the negative prefix and is used of ladders, feet, hands, and voices.
items.cn: unsteady 由否定前缀构成，用于梯子、脚步、手与声音。

items.en: The figurative senses grow in economics and politics, where unsteady means not dependable.
items.cn: 此后词义在经济学与政治中扩展出比喻用法，指「靠不住」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the stead family and its near neighbours in spelling, while the near-meaning group collects unstable words.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 stead 词族及拼写相近者，近义组汇集表示不稳定动摇的词。

entries.definition: firm and not moving
at a constant rate
firmness of position
in the place of another thing
not neat or orderly
entries.definitionCN: 不整洁的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: moving from side to side
trembling or weak
likely to change or fall
solid and not moving

normalIntro.en: The word rests on an old English noun for a place to stand, which still survives in everyday phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词压在一个古老的英语名词「落脚处」上，这个名词今天仍活在日常短语里。

normal.en: Un- plus steady: steady goes back to stead, a place to stand.
normal.cn: un- 加 steady：steady 源自 stead，意为「落脚处」。

normal.en: Unsteady on one's feet is the most useful phrase for illness and age.
normal.cn: unsteady on one's feet 是谈论病弱与年老时最好用的说法。

normal.en: An unsteady hand and an unsteady voice keep the physical image for feeling.
normal.cn: an unsteady hand 与 an unsteady voice 把身体的画面留给情绪。

normal.en: The noun is unsteadiness, the adverb unsteadily.
normal.cn: 名词是 unsteadiness，副词是 unsteadily。

normal.en: Instead and steady both contain stead, though their senses differ.
normal.cn: instead 与 steady 都含 stead，但意思不同。

abstract.en: See a table shake because one leg lacks a small block.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子因一条腿缺了块小木片而晃。

abstract.en: Feel a hand on a rail after a long illness.
abstract.cn: 体会久病之后扶住栏杆的那只手。

abstract.en: Hear a voice rise and fall in the middle of a sentence.
abstract.cn: 听一句话说到中途声音忽高忽低。

examples.en: The old chair is unsteady, so do not lean on the back.
examples.cn: 这把旧椅子不稳，别往后靠。

examples.en: Her unsteady hand made the signature look strange.
examples.cn: 她发抖的手让签名看起来很奇怪。

examples.en: Growth in the sector has been unsteady since the spring.
examples.cn: 这个行业的增长自开春以来起伏不定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺得死地」——脚下这块地若稳当，俺才敢站；找不着这样的地，身子就一直晃。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ steady（稳的），steady 源自晚期古英语 stedig，词根为 stede（地方、位置），与 stand 同出日耳曼语族

sensesIntro.en: One root idea, having no firm place, starts with furniture and feet and ends with markets and loyalty.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个根义「没有稳当的落脚处」，从家具与脚步一路走到市场与忠诚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface that shifts under whatever rests on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：放在上面的东西一动就跟着晃。

branches.en: The physical branch: legs, ladders, and tables that move.
branches.cn: 实体分支：会动的桌腿、梯子与桌子。

branches.en: The balance branch: a body that cannot hold itself up.
branches.cn: 平衡分支：撑不住自己的身子。

branches.en: The trembling branch: hands and voices that shake.
branches.cn: 颤动分支：发抖的手与嗓音。

branches.en: The trend branch: numbers that will not stay level.
branches.cn: 走势分支：起起伏伏的数字。

branches.en: The loyalty branch: support that may tip at any time.
branches.cn: 忠诚分支：随时可能倒向一边的支持。

intro.en: A native negative prefix over an adjective built on a noun that English has had for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在由一个英语已用了上千年的名词所作的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The word is not Latin; the nearest Latin relative of the idea is stabilis, standing firm.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词并非拉丁语；概念上最近似的拉丁词是 stabilis（站得稳的）。

items.example: He came in his brother's stead.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.example: He rose unsteadily to his feet.

definition_zh: 抵抗的；有抵抗力的；耐……的
definition_en: not easily harmed or affected by something, or opposing something
core_image: 一层看不见的铠甲，把水、火或细菌挡在外面
scene: 这种布经过处理，不容易被水浸湿。 This cloth is treated to be resistant to water.
sceneCN: 这里 resistant 是「耐……的」（第 1 个义项：不容易受到某物影响或伤害）；句意：这种布经过处理，能防水。

pos.zh: 抵抗的；有抵抗力的；耐……的

derivatives.zh: 抵抗；抵制
抵抗；阻力
电阻器

senses.title: Not easily harmed by something
senses.definition: strong enough to remain undamaged or unaffected by a substance or condition
senses.definitionCN: 足够坚固，面对某种物质或条件仍不受损、不受影响
senses.example: This cloth is treated to be resistant to water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种布经过处理，能防水。
senses.why: The -ant adjective describes the quality shown by something that resists.
senses.whyCN: -ant 形容词描述某物抵抗时所展现的性质。

senses.title: Opposing change or control
senses.definition: unwilling to accept a change, idea, or authority
senses.definitionCN: 不愿接受变化、观念或权威
senses.example: The committee was resistant to change.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会抗拒变革。
senses.why: The same standing-against quality appears in human attitudes.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「顶住」性质出现在人的态度中。

senses.title: Able to withstand a drug
senses.definition: used of germs that are no longer harmed by a medicine
senses.definitionCN: 用于指不再被药物伤害的病菌
senses.example: Drug-resistant bacteria are a growing concern.
senses.exampleCN: 耐药细菌日益令人担忧。
senses.why: A germ that stands against medicine is resistant in the medical sense.
senses.whyCN: 顶住药物的病菌，就是医学意义上的「耐药」。

intro.en: Resistant is the present participle of Latin resistere, to stand against, used as an English adjective.
intro.cn: resistant 是拉丁语 resistere（站到对面）的现在分词，在英语中作形容词。

items.en: Sistere means to take a stand.
items.cn: sistere 意为站定。

items.en: Resistere means to stand against.
items.cn: resistere 意为站到对面。

items.en: Resister means to resist.
items.cn: resister 意为抵抗。

items.en: Resist settles into English as the base verb.
items.cn: resist 作为基础动词进入英语。

items.en: Resistant appears as an adjective of quality.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，resistant 作为性质形容词出现。

items.en: Modern English uses resistant for water, heat, drugs, and change.
items.cn: 现代英语中，resistant 用于水、热、药物与变化。

note.en: Resistant is the adjective of resist, and it sits near its family and near words for immunity and toughness.
note.cn: resistant 是 resist 的形容词，与自身词族以及表示免疫和坚韧的词相邻。

entries.definition: to fight against something
the act of resisting or a force against motion
a device that limits current
protected from a disease or effect
strong and not easily damaged
strongly against something

normalIntro.en: Resistant is resist plus -ant: showing the quality of standing against something.
normalIntro.cn: resistant 是 resist 加 -ant：表现出顶住某物的性质。

normal.en: Resistant to is the fixed pattern.
normal.cn: resistant to 是固定搭配。

normal.en: Water-resistant cloth keeps rain out for a while.
normal.cn: 防水布能暂时挡住雨水。

normal.en: Heat-resistant materials survive high temperatures.
normal.cn: 耐热材料能承受高温。

normal.en: People can be resistant to change.
normal.cn: 人可能抗拒变化。

normal.en: Compare immune: immune means fully protected, while resistant means able to withstand.
normal.cn: 对比 immune：immune 指完全免疫，resistant 指能够抵挡。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible coat shedding drops of water.
abstract.cn: 想象一件看不见的外衣让水珠滑落。

abstract.en: Imagine a shield taking a blow without cracking.
abstract.cn: 想象盾牌受击却不裂开。

abstract.en: Think of weeds pushing back through pavement.
abstract.cn: 想象杂草从路面缝隙里顶出来。

examples.en: This cloth is treated to be resistant to water.
examples.cn: 这种布经过处理，能防水。

examples.en: The committee was resistant to change.
examples.cn: 委员会抗拒变革。

examples.en: Drug-resistant bacteria are a growing concern.
examples.cn: 耐药细菌日益令人担忧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「resist + ant」——身上带着顶住的劲儿，就是有抵抗力的；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sistere（站定）→ resistere（站到对面）→ 古法语 resister → 英语 resist ＋ -ant → resistant。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective describes whatever can stand against harm: a fabric against water, a person against change, a germ against medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词描述能顶住伤害的事物：布料防水、人抗拒变化、病菌耐药。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible armour that keeps a threat outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层看不见的铠甲，把威胁挡在外面。

branches.en: Materials that withstand water or heat are the basic sense.
branches.cn: 防水耐热的材料，是基本义项。

branches.en: People who oppose change show the same quality.
branches.cn: 抗拒变化的人表现出同样的性质。

branches.en: Germs that survive medicine are resistant in the medical sense.
branches.cn: 在药物下存活的病菌，是医学意义上的耐药。

branches.en: Cloth and bacteria both keep a harmful substance out.
branches.cn: 布料与细菌都把有害物质挡在外面。

branches.en: An attitude and a germ can both refuse to give way.
branches.cn: 态度与病菌都可以拒绝让步。

intro.en: Resistant is an English -ant adjective built on the Latin verb resistere.
intro.cn: resistant 是建立在拉丁动词 resistere 上的英语 -ant 形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere means to take a stand, and resistere means to stand against.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere 意为站定，resistere 意为站到对面。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of pushing back.
items.exampleCN: re- 增添「顶回去」的意思。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或动作的词尾

definition_zh: 同伴；伴侣；配对物；指南
definition_en: a person who spends time with you or travels with you, or a thing that goes with another
core_image: 旅途中并肩走着的两个人，一左一右踩着同一段影子
scene: 雨夜里，老人把伞往同伴那边偏了偏。 He walked slowly so his companion could keep up.
sceneCN: 这里 companion 指「同伴」（第 1 个义项：与你同行的人）；句意是他放慢脚步，好让同伴跟上。

derivatives.zh: 陪伴；友谊
友善合群的
亲切地
陪伴；伴随
伴随物；伴奏

senses.title: A person who goes with you
senses.definition: a person who spends time with you or goes somewhere with you
senses.definitionCN: 与你共度时光或一同前往某处的人
senses.example: Her dog was her only companion on long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 长距离散步时，她的狗是唯一的同伴。
senses.why: A companion is defined by shared time, not by a shared address.
senses.whyCN: 同伴由共度的时光来定义，而不是由同一个住址来定义。

senses.title: A thing that matches another
senses.definition: one of a pair of things that are designed to go together
senses.definitionCN: 设计上成对、配套使用的事物之一
senses.example: This book is a companion to the earlier dictionary.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是早前那部词典的配套卷。
senses.why: Objects, like people, can be paired so that each answers the other.
senses.whyCN: 物件和人都能配对，彼此呼应。

senses.title: A handbook for a place
senses.definition: a book that gives information for visitors or users
senses.definitionCN: 为访客或使用者提供信息的书
senses.example: He bought a companion to the old city.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一本古城指南。
senses.why: A guide walks beside you in words, so it is called a companion.
senses.whyCN: 指南用文字陪你走，所以也被叫作 companion。

intro.en: Companion comes from Latin com, together, and panis, bread: a companion was the person who shared your bread.
intro.cn: companion 来自拉丁语 com（一起）与 panis（面包）：companion 本指与你分面包的人。

items.en: Com panis described one who ate bread with another.
items.cn: com panis 指与另一个人一同吃面包的人。

items.en: Companio named a fellow soldier who shared the daily ration.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 companio 指分食每日口粮的战友。

items.en: Old French compaignon widened the word to any comrade.
items.cn: 古法语 compaignon 把这个词扩展到任何伙伴。

items.en: English companion first meant a person who shared a journey.
items.cn: 英语 companion 最初指共走一段路的人。

items.en: It grew to cover matching books and travel guides.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到配套的书与旅行指南。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to companion, and the meaning group names other people or things that stay beside you.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 companion 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他陪伴在侧的人或物。

entries.definition: the state of being with someone
friendly and easy to be with
to go somewhere with someone
a person who does something with you
a friend who shares your work or beliefs
a friend or a life partner

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with shared bread, then move to shared roads and to the books that walk beside us.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从分面包开始，再走到同行的路与陪我们走的手册。

normal.en: Com- is together and pan- is bread, so a companion is a bread mate.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pan- 是面包，companion 就是分面包的人。

normal.en: A companion shares your time, not necessarily your home.
normal.cn: 同伴分享的是你的时间，不一定是你的住处。

normal.en: A companion volume is a book paired with another book.
normal.cn: 配套卷就是与另一本书成对的书。

normal.en: A travel guide is a companion because it goes with you.
normal.cn: 旅行指南是 companion，因为它跟着你走。

normal.en: Companionship is the warm noun behind the person.
normal.cn: companionship 是这个人背后那个温暖的抽象名词。

abstract.en: Picture two walkers under one umbrella in the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨中两个人同撑一把伞。

abstract.en: Picture a dog waiting by the door every evening.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗每天傍晚在门口等候。

abstract.en: Picture two books standing side by side on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象两本书并排立在书架上。

examples.en: Her sister was her closest companion during the trip.
examples.cn: 旅途中她妹妹是她最亲近的同伴。

examples.en: The old man's companion was a small grey cat.
examples.cn: 老人的伴侣是一只小灰猫。

examples.en: This workbook is a companion to the main text.
examples.cn: 这本练习册是主教材的配套用书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 companion 记成 com（一起）加 pan（面包）加 ion：一起分面包的人，就是同伴。

root: 源自拉丁语 com（一起）与 panis（面包），本义是一同吃面包的人，后引申为同伴、配对之物与指南。

sensesIntro.en: From the person who shares your bread, to the thing that pairs with another, and finally to the guidebook that travels with you.
sensesIntro.cn: 从与你分面包的人，到与另一物配对的东西，最后到陪你上路的手册。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two travellers walking side by side, their shadows joined on one road.
core.cn: 核心意象：旅途中并肩走着的两个人，一左一右踩着同一段影子。

branches.en: The oldest sense is the person who shares daily bread.
branches.cn: 最古老的义项是与你分食日常面包的人。

branches.en: A matching object answers the first like a second voice.
branches.cn: 配对之物像第二个声音一样回应第一个。

branches.en: A guidebook is a companion made of paper.
branches.cn: 指南是用纸做的同伴。

branches.en: Person and object both keep someone from being alone.
branches.cn: 人和物都在让人不至于孤单。

branches.en: A companion volume and a guide both complete a set.
branches.cn: 配套卷与指南都让一套东西变得完整。

intro.en: Companion is built on Latin com, together, plus panis, bread.
intro.cn: companion 由拉丁语 com（一起）加 panis（面包）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin bread base pan- also gives us pantry and pannier.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的面包词基 pan- 还给出了 pantry 与 pannier 这样的词。

items.example: They sat companionably by the fire.
items.exampleCN: 他们亲切地坐在炉火旁。

items.example: A teacher must accompany the class.

items.meaning: something that goes with another thing
items.example: Music was the accompaniment to the meal.
The accompanying notes explain the chart.
